_comment: Audited official programme facts, applied only to records whose official source host matches exactly.
_rules: Only facts verified on the awarding body's own page during a live research pass are listed. Anything marked unverified in the research was left out rather than guessed.
A facts entry only fills a field that is currently NULL. It never overwrites a value the scraper already read from the official page, because the page is the fresher source.
Deadlines are cycle-specific. Each entry states the cycle it was verified against so a stale value is recognisable rather than silently presented as current.
Amounts are the awarding body's published figure for that cycle and are labelled per_cycle where the value can change year to year.
Matching is by exact official source host. A record from chevening.org cannot pick up Commonwealth facts, so a wrong entry cannot be applied to the wrong programme.

id:45.application_link: https://www.education.gov.au/research-block-grants/research-training-program (department page; instructs applicants to contact the chosen university directly)
id:45.benefits: Not a fixed award amount. The Department funds higher education providers through Research Block Grants; "RTP scholarships can be offered for a period of 3 to 4 years for students studying research doctorates, and for up to 2 years for students studying research masters degrees." (source: https://www.education.gov.au/research-block-grants)

id:47.eligibility: Must be a citizen of a country with a **GDP per capita of US$10,000 or less** (World Bank data; see the page's "Eligible countries" list); must hold an offer for an Overseas Fee place in a bachelor's degree for the year the scholarship is offered; must not have previously undertaken tertiary studies (excluding extension studies completed as part of a Year 12 program).
id:47.description: Awarded to talented international students enrolling in a bachelor's degree who are citizens of countries where international educational opportunities are limited by financial disadvantage. Selection is based on final secondary school or foundation study results (not predicted results); selection scores are reviewed annually. Successful candidates are notified within five working days of receiving a course offer.
id:47.benefits: **20% fee sponsorship** for the duration of the course from 2027 (awards made before 2027 were 25%). Quantity: at least 110, increasing to **225** from 2027. Stated benefit amount: "20% fee remission".

american.edu.official_source: American University (Office of Enrollment Services, Washington, DC)
american.edu.eligibility: International students needing a non-immigrant F-1 or J-1 visa. **Not eligible** if: US citizen, US permanent resident, US pending permanent resident, or dual US citizen; enrolled in or already begun post-secondary study at another university; graduated secondary school earlier than 2024; not finishing high school by June 2027. Must also meet AU's academic and English-proficiency requirements. Preference given to students who have overcome obstacles / from diverse and underrepresented global and socioeconomic backgrounds, who show commitment to leadership, volunteerism and community service, and who meet English requirements.
american.edu.description: Two-step application: (1) submit the Common Application plus all international supporting documents, and (2) submit the AU EGLS application and essays via the applicant portal — **both by 15 January 2027**; Step 1 must be completed first and late applications are not considered. Applicants must upload a bank letter and signed AU Declaration of Finances Form each confirming a minimum of USD 4,000, plus official TOEFL/IELTS/DET/PTE/LanguageCERT/Cambridge scores sent directly by the testing agency. AU recommends Regular Decision for Fall 2027; finalists and award winners are notified by **1 April 2027**. Scholarships do not guarantee visa issuance.
american.edu.benefits: Full AU Emerging Global Leader Scholarship covers **all billable AU expenses (full tuition, room and board)** for **2 international students**; renewable for a total of **4 years** of undergraduate study on continued satisfactory academic performance. Additional **AU EGL Partial Scholarships valued at up to USD 40,000 per year** are also offered, selected from applicants who complete the EGLS process. Non-billable costs (mandatory health insurance, books, airfare, taxes, misc.) are **not** covered — approximately **USD 4,000 per year** payable by the student.

admissions.tc.umn.edu.official_source: University of Minnesota Twin Cities — Office of Admissions (Office of Enrollment Management)
admissions.tc.umn.edu.eligibility: All international students who apply for admission by the freshman or transfer application deadlines **and** complete the Certification of Finances Form. Admitted freshmen on F-1 or valid non-immigrant status (H-4, L-2, E-2, TD). Not eligible if the student qualifies for Minnesota Resident tuition rates through approved residency or reciprocity with Minnesota, Wisconsin, North Dakota or Manitoba.
admissions.tc.umn.edu.benefits: Tuition-only. Not applicable to study-abroad programmes. Requires maintaining full-time enrolment (≥12 credits/semester) and valid non-immigrant visa status; not tied to a particular major or college; award cannot be increased mid-degree. Freshmen **$5,000–$20,000 per year for up to four years**; transfer students **$10,000 per year for up to three years** (fall entry only; spring transfer considered on a funds-available basis). The award "provides up to four-years of an undergraduate non-resident tuition waiver that can be applied only toward tuition costs."
admissions.tc.umn.edu.degree: Undergraduate — incoming freshmen and transfer students
admissions.tc.umn.edu.description: Competitive merit-based scholarship awarded automatically to admitted international freshmen and transfer students who file the Certification of Finances Form by the standard admission deadlines. A very limited number of awards are made each year; freshmen recipients are notified by the end of March and transfer recipients in May–June.

clarku.edu.official_source: Clark University — Office of Financial Assistance
clarku.edu.eligibility: Merit-based decisions are made **solely** on the admission application, with no consideration of financial need. All applicants are automatically considered. Finalists are selected and invited to interview. Awarded to approximately **five** students annually.
clarku.edu.description: Clark University's Presidential Scholarship is a merit-based award recognising outstanding academic achievement and leadership potential; recipients are among the top applicants to Clark. Admitted students who receive merit-based scholarships are notified at the time of admission.
clarku.edu.benefits: Covers **full tuition plus on-campus housing and meals for all four years**, regardless of a family's financial situation.

isss.uoregon.edu.official_source: University of Oregon — International Student & Scholar Services (Division of Global Engagement)
isss.uoregon.edu.eligibility: New and continuing international students at the University of Oregon.
isss.uoregon.edu.benefits: Renewable annually until completion of a UO degree, contingent on fulfilling ICSP programme requirements. Participants present to local schools and community organisations as cross-cultural ambassadors. A **partial tuition-waiver scholarship covering approximately half the student's tuition** (the page states the scholarship covers "approximately half their tuition").
isss.uoregon.edu.degree: undergraduate (until completion of a UO degree)
isss.uoregon.edu.description: ICSP recipients serve as cross-cultural ambassadors in the Eugene-Springfield area, leading presentations about their home culture in local schools and community organisations. Obligation is **66–80 hours of cultural service per year** — speaking or demonstrating aspects of their country's heritage and culture to schools or community groups, or engaging in international campus events. The programme has a 35-year alumni history.

id:71.official_source: University College London (UCL Scholarships and funding)
id:71.eligibility: candidates from any country outside the UK; eligible to pay the Overseas fee rate; from a lower-income background; a complete UCL admission application (including references) submitted for a full-time Master's degree in 2026/27. Distance-learning options are not eligible.
id:71.benefits: up to 85 scholarships in 2026/27, with 5 ring-fenced for students from India and 1 for a student from Japan (the Japan award forms part of the Musubi Global Master's Scholarship). Applied first to tuition fees, remainder paid to the recipient in three equal instalments through the academic year towards maintenance. Tenable for one year (50% per year for 2-year programmes). May be held alongside other funding subject to total value.
id:71.description: Enables and encourages international students from lower-income backgrounds to pursue full-time Master's degree studies at UCL; awarded on financial need. Shortlisted candidates are contacted mid-May to provide evidence of financial need; successful candidates typically informed by late June.

id:72.official_source: University College London (UCL Scholarships and funding)
id:72.eligibility: candidates from any country outside the UK (applications not accepted from those already residing in the UK); at serious risk as a direct result of armed conflict and/or displaced within or forced to leave their home country within the last three years because of armed conflict and having sought international protection outside the UK; eligible for the Overseas fee rate; from a lower-income background; not already holding or gaining a qualification at the level applied for; must hold an offer of a place on a chosen full-time UCL Master's by the scholarship panel meeting at the start of June 2026; must have valid travel documents in place. Distance-learning and part-time Master's are not eligible.
id:72.benefits: up to 3 scholarships in 2026/27; a single room in UCL accommodation is guaranteed if the recipient takes it up (the accommodation fee is deducted from the £20,000); may **not** be held alongside other scholarships, studentships, awards or bursaries full tuition fees + a maintenance payment of approx. £20,000 covering accommodation and living costs for the normal course duration + an allowance for the Immigration Health Surcharge, visa fees and one return flight
id:72.description: Enables students at serious risk and/or displaced due to armed conflict to pursue full-time Master's degree studies at UCL; awarded on financial need upon the recommendation of the UCL Humanitarian Scholarship panel. UCL notes that, under recent UK Government legislation, citizens of Cameroon, Sudan, Myanmar and Afghanistan cannot obtain a Study Visa to enter the UK from 26 March 2026.

futurestudents.yorku.ca.eligibility: International high-school applicants entering the first year of an undergraduate degree at York; hold international student status and be subject to international tuition fees; demonstrate strong academic performance, leadership and active involvement in volunteer work/extracurricular activities; **minimum final admission average of 80% (A) or equivalent**; must be officially nominated by a guidance counsellor, principal or senior school official, with a **maximum of two nominations per school per year**. Applicants do not need an offer of admission to apply. A 9-digit York reference number (issued within 4–5 business days of applying) is required; admission applications after 19 January 2027 may not be eligible.
futurestudents.yorku.ca.benefits: Matched with mentors from day one who support the transition to university and connect scholars to resources; complimentary registration for York's annual Career Ready Conference each year of study; exclusive engagement opportunities with senior leaders and professors across faculties. **CAD $180,000** total, valued at **CAD $45,000 per year** over four years; renewable for three additional years of full-time undergraduate study while maintaining good academic standing. It is a high-value award that **cannot be combined with entrance scholarships** — students receive the higher of the two.
futurestudents.yorku.ca.description: Awarded to international high-school applicants who demonstrate academic excellence, commitment to volunteer work and extracurricular activities, and leadership skills; recipients are referred to as President's International Scholars and are drawn from a variety of regions around the world.

uwaterloo.ca.eligibility: International fee-paying students admitted to a full-time, first-year degree programme at Waterloo. Students applying from CEGEP are eligible. The scholarship is available in most undergraduate programmes (with listed exceptions). The student must still meet the eligibility criteria when they start in first year, and deferred admission is permitted with the scholarship applied when they begin. There are **no limits on the number of recipients** — all students meeting the criteria receive it. Not available if the student's residency status changes so they are no longer liable for higher international study permit tuition fees. Students receiving an Ontario Student Assistance Program (OSAP) loan are in most cases Canadian citizens/Permanent Residents/Protected Persons and therefore ineligible.
uwaterloo.ca.benefits: Can be received **in addition to** any other entrance scholarship from Waterloo (including President's and Merit scholarships) and does not replace or reduce them. Cannot be applied to more than one year. **CAD $10,000** for first-year studies, disbursed in two instalments of $5,000 — the first in **late July** toward first-term tuition, the second in **late November** toward second-term tuition. It can be applied only to the first- and second-term tuition fee bills and **cannot** be transferred directly to the student. No specific GPA is required beyond the minimum conditions of the Offer of Admission.
uwaterloo.ca.description: Waterloo's automatic International Student Entrance Scholarship, a $10,000 tuition credit for international fee-paying students entering their first year of most undergraduate programmes, awarded without any separate application. Waterloo lists it alongside the Mathematics International Awards for India students (up to 15, valued $20,000–$40,000) and Faculty of Science International Student scholarships (15 awards of $25,000–$80,000) as further options for international students.

id:101.official_source: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) — A*STAR Graduate Academy
id:101.eligibility: Open to applicants of all nationalities. International students must have completed or be on track to obtain a Bachelor's or Master's degree at a Singapore autonomous university, with at least a Second-Class (Upper) Honours degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline; be in the last semester of their final studies; and satisfy the criteria for and gain admission to a PhD programme in an autonomous university. Mid-Term AGS applicants must already be enrolled at a Singapore autonomous university and have completed at least one semester.
id:101.benefits: Support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment; specialised higher-stipend tracks in Semiconductor, Quantum and Computing. Up to 4 years; bond-free for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents. Full tuition fees plus a monthly sustenance allowance (inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable). International-student monthly allowance: **AGS (STEM) SGD 3,600**; **AGS (Specialised Tracks — Semiconductor, Quantum, Computing) SGD 5,000**. Also book, computer, conference and thesis allowances. Rates are subject to A*STAR adjustment.
id:101.degree: PhD at a Singapore autonomous university; four tracks (STEM, Semiconductor, Quantum, Computing)
id:101.description: A*STAR funds up to four years of PhD study at a Singapore autonomous university across four tracks. Scholars are jointly supervised by an A*STAR researcher and a university supervisor.

id:102.official_source: National University of Singapore — NUS Graduate School
id:102.eligibility: PhD Students and Master's (Research) Students. Nationalities: Singapore Citizens, Singapore Permanent Residents, all International Students. Undergraduate degree with at least Second Class Honours (Upper division) / Honours (Distinction) or equivalent. Strong statement of purpose, letters of recommendation and CV compulsory; GRE, publications and TOEFL/IELTS optional but strengthening.
id:102.benefits: increased amount of SGD 500/month after passing the PhD Qualifying Examination; no specific service bond; International Students on the Scholarship must fulfil the Graduate Assistantship Programme requirements. Monthly stipend — Singapore Citizens: SGD 3,800 (PhD and MSc Research); Singapore Permanent Residents: SGD 3,400 (PhD) / SGD 3,000 (MSc Research); all International Students: SGD 3,000 (PhD) / SGD 2,900 (MSc Research). **Full waiver of tuition fees.** Rates take effect from 1 January 2026. CPF is given on top of the stipend for Singapore Citizens.
id:102.description: Awarded to outstanding graduate students for research leading to a higher degree at the University. Tenable for one year in the first instance, renewable each semester at the University's discretion; maximum two years for Master's candidates and four years for PhD candidates. Scholars may not hold any other employment, scholarship, award, fellowship or allowance without prior university approval. Enquiries: nusgsenquiry@nus.edu.sg

id:103.official_source: National University of Singapore — NUS Graduate School (Commonwealth Scholarship)
id:103.eligibility: Commonwealth citizens only. For new, incoming students who are **not** Singapore citizens or permanent residents. Undergraduate degree with at least Second Class Honours (Upper Division) / Honours (Distinction) or equivalent. Candidate must first be eligible for MOE Subsidy.
id:103.benefits: PhD scholars may receive an additional stipend of up to SGD 500/month upon passing the PhD Qualifying Examination (normally 12–18 months after registration of candidature), renewable each semester subject to good performance; quantum and duration may vary between Faculties and Schools. Typical award period: 4 years (PhD), 2 years (Master's Research). No specific service bond. Monthly stipend — Commonwealth Students: SGD 3,000 (PhD) / SGD 2,900 (Master's Research). Subsidy for full tuition fees at the University. Rates take effect from 1 January 2026.
id:103.description: Awarded to outstanding graduate students from Commonwealth countries for research leading to a higher degree at the University; a number of students are selected each semester by the University. A number of students are selected each semester. Tenable one year in the first instance, renewable each semester; maximum two years for Master's candidates and four years for PhD candidates.

id:104.official_source: National University of Singapore — NUS Graduate School
id:104.eligibility: PhD Students. Nationalities: Singapore Citizens, Singapore Permanent Residents, all International Students. No specific academic pre-requisites. Excellent PhD applicants must be **nominated by the Faculty/Department**; application procedures are advised once the applicant is assessed eligible. Preference given to candidates who exhibit leadership ability and commitment to community service.
id:104.benefits: typical award period 4 years; tenable one year in the first instance and renewable each semester at the University's discretion. No specific service bond. The Fellowship is funded by the Lee Kong Chian Scholarship. Monthly stipend — Singapore Citizens: SGD 4,800; Singapore Permanent Residents: SGD 4,400; All International Students: SGD 3,900. CPF is given on top of the stipend for Singapore Citizens (published CPF amounts: SC SGD 4,800, PR SGD 4,400). Full waiver of tuition fees.
id:104.description: Awarded to candidates who show exceptional promise or accomplishment in research; a number of PhD research students are selected each semester by the University. Successful applicants are informed of the outcome sometime in May (for admission in August) or October (for admission in January) and must sign a letter of undertaking.

id:105.official_source: National University of Singapore, Office of Admissions
id:105.eligibility: citizens of all countries except Singapore; strong leadership qualities and potential; outstanding co-curricular activities record; outstanding high school results; applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS; transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are **not** eligible
id:105.benefits: tenable for the normal candidature period and transferable across programmes; renewed every semester provided GPA ≥3.5 (or top 80% of cohort for Dentistry/Law/Medicine) and good conduct; includes Double and Joint Degree Programmes 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees (after the MOE Tuition Grant, which recipients must take up) + S$5,800 annual living allowance + S$1,750 one-time computer allowance upon enrolment + S$5,000 annual accommodation allowance
id:105.description: A university-level scholarship supporting exceptional international students from all countries except Singapore with outstanding achievements, renewable on academic performance.

icar.gov.in.official_source: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India — Agricultural Education Division
icar.gov.in.eligibility: Indian **and** overseas nationals holding a Master's degree in Agriculture and Allied Sciences, applying for a doctoral degree in the identified priority areas. Fresh candidates and in-service candidates (with deputation permission from the parent organisation). ICAR reserves the right to verify certificates; applicants from India and the People's Republic of China are asked to submit an APS Certificate.
icar.gov.in.benefits: first instalment (first six months) released on acceptance and host-university admission letter; subsequent instalments released against certified academic progress reports; an in-service fellow may continue to receive salary/leave/benefits from the parent organisation. PhD amount — Indian fellows going abroad: **USD 2,000 per month** plus lump-sum contingent/preparatory expenses **up to USD 1,000 per year**; overseas fellows in India: **INR 40,000 per month** plus lump sum **up to INR 25,000 per year**. Plus to-and-fro economy-class air ticket provided by the Council for both categories, and economy-class travel cost reimbursement from the port of arrival in India to the destination university and back for overseas fellows. The fellow bears all other costs including medical insurance. Indian fellows must provide an irrevocable bank guarantee of USD 10,000; for foreign nationals INR 2,00,000 is recovered from the grant.
icar.gov.in.degree: PhD (doctoral degree in Agriculture and Allied Sciences) — **30 fellowships of three years** for the 2026 cycle
icar.gov.in.description: Programme landing page: https://www.icar.gov.in/netaji-subhas-icar-international-fellowship (page last updated 30-09-2026); it hosts only the announcement PDF. The record's URL https://www.icar.gov.in is the ICAR homepage, i.e. a parent page rather than a programme-specific one.

ousf.duke.edu.official_source: Duke University — Office of University Scholars and Fellows (OUSF)
ousf.duke.edu.eligibility: any country outside the U.S.; no dual U.S./other citizenship; no pre-existing B.A. or B.S. degree; strong academic preparation and documented need for financial aid; complete financial-aid forms (CSS Profile / FAFSA via Duke Financial Aid). Nominated scholars are accepted; candidates cannot be nominated.
ousf.duke.edu.description: The Karsh International Scholarship was founded in 2010 through a donation from Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh. Karsh International Scholars form an intellectually and civically engaged cohort of international students promoting interdisciplinary inquiry, academic research and scholarship in the service of society. The current cohort includes students from Botswana, Bulgaria, Chile, Egypt, England, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Madagascar, Mongolia, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Pakistan, Russia, Rwanda, South Africa, Syria, Tajikistan, Thailand, Tunisia, Vietnam and Zimbabwe.
ousf.duke.edu.benefits: tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need exceeding those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships and other academic-career opportunities

admissions.yale.edu.official_source: Yale University — Yale College, Office of Undergraduate Financial Aid (page hosted on admissions.yale.edu)
admissions.yale.edu.eligibility: Aid is need-blind at admission and need-based in award — "regardless of a student's citizenship or immigration status". International students interested in need-based aid must indicate interest on the admissions application (Common App, Coalition App or QuestBridge); Undergraduate Financial Aid then contacts them directly with the required documents. Yale does **not** accept the International Student Financial Aid Application (ISFAA).
admissions.yale.edu.benefits: need is assessed holistically (income, assets, family size, unique circumstances); loans are not included in initial aid offers; families whose aid application becomes complete after an admissions decision are still eligible and offers are not reduced. All financial aid is awarded as **scholarships (grants), not loans**, and aid offers meet 100% of demonstrated need. Published figures on the page: average annual need-based scholarship **$75,220**; 88% of Yale College graduates with no student loan debt; 21% of students whose families pay nothing to attend; no cost for families with incomes below $100,000 and typical assets, no tuition for families below $200,000 and typical assets.
admissions.yale.edu.description: Yale awards every dollar of undergraduate financial aid on the basis of demonstrated financial need, without requiring loans. The recorded page (https://admissions.yale.edu/affordability) is live and on the awarding body's own domain but **states no deadline**; the priority deadlines above come from Yale's Office of Undergraduate Financial Aid site.

akf.org.official_source: Aga Khan Foundation (AKF), an agency of the Aga Khan Development Network
akf.org.eligibility: excellent academic record; Bachelor's degree or equivalent training/professional experience; genuine financial need; a thoughtful, reliable multi-source funding plan covering all years of study; admission to a reputable postgraduate institution; starting the **first year** of the programme; strong leadership potential, professional experience, extracurricular/entrepreneurial achievements and volunteer contributions. Preference is given to young professionals under 30. Available to nationals of selected countries (incl. Afghanistan, Australia, Bangladesh, Egypt, India, Kenya, Kyrgyz Republic, Madagascar, Mozambique, New Zealand, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda) and, in some countries (e.g. Canada, Portugal, USA), to those originally from a listed country. Not available to students who wish to study in the **United Kingdom or Russia**.
akf.org.benefits: does **not** cover international travel, clothing, furniture, or living expenses for family members. Maintenance requires continued good academic standing and ongoing financial need. A guarantor must co-sign the award agreement; repayment of the loan component plus a service charge begins six months after the first of: graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support for failing the required academic standards. structured as **half grant and half loan** — 50% of the award must be repaid. Covers tuition expenses and student living expenses.
akf.org.degree: Master's (priority given) and PhD (funded for the first two years only; applicant then expected to find alternative funding). Local/regional universities and distance-learning programmes are acceptable if course quality is maintained; part-time and short courses are not considered.
akf.org.description: Postgraduate scholarship established in 1969 by His Highness the Aga Khan IV that has supported more than 1,500 students. AKF offers a limited number of new awards each cycle and treats the ISP as a "resource of last resort", expecting applicants to secure multiple funding sources.

youarewelcomehereusa.org.official_source: #YouAreWelcomeHere — a scholarship and social-media campaign of NAFSA: Association of International Educators (1425 K Street NW, Suite 1200, Washington, DC 20005). NAFSA coordinates; each participating U.S. institution selects and awards its own scholars.
youarewelcomehereusa.org.eligibility: first-year international applicant in any field of study to a participating college or university; an "international applicant" holds citizenship of a country outside the U.S. and does **not** also hold U.S. citizenship or permanent residency; demonstrates interest and initiative in promoting intercultural learning and exchange; must also meet that institution's admission criteria and deadlines; must complete the YAWH scholarship application plus a 500–1,000 word essay or a two-to-five minute video answering: "Tell us about your leadership skills in your school or community, and how you plan to continue applying your leadership skills at the U.S. institution you are applying to." Some participating institutions accept essays only.
youarewelcomehereusa.org.benefits: renewable for the length of the degree programme — maximum 2 years for an associate's degree, maximum 4 years for a bachelor's degree — provided the student makes satisfactory academic progress as determined by the institution. Participation commitment is renewed annually by the institution. each participating college or university offers **two annual, renewable scholarships covering a minimum of 50 % of published annual out-of-state tuition costs (excluding fees)**, funded entirely with institutional money. The scholarships are additive — not relabelled awards and not drawn from pre-existing scholarship funds.
youarewelcomehereusa.org.description: #YouAreWelcomeHere began as a grassroots campaign among U.S. higher education institutions and has spread to 480 institutions, organisations and secondary schools; nearly 50 universities committed to offering scholarships in 2026. All questions about an individual award are directed to the participating institution, not to NAFSA. The 2024 scholar class included 22 students from 17 countries at 13 U.S. institutions.

investyourtalentapplication.esteri.it.official_source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI) — Invest Your Talent in Italy, with ICE – Italian Trade Agency and Uni-Italia
investyourtalentapplication.esteri.it.eligibility: Citizens permanently resident in one of the 22 eligible countries (Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, India, Indonesia, Iran, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Mongolia, Paraguay, Peru, People's Republic of China, Tunisia, Türkiye, Uruguay, Vietnam). Must hold a qualification valid for a Master's/Postgraduate programme; **students who are about to graduate are not eligible**; students currently studying at, or already graduated from, an Italian university are **not** eligible. Born on or after **1 January 2000** (except renewals). Must submit a pre-admission application to an IYT-listed course, and English **B2 CEFR** or higher, plus Italian certification or a commitment to study Italian. Only one course (max two preferences for limited-enrolment courses). One application only.
investyourtalentapplication.esteri.it.degree: Master's (Laurea Magistrale) and Postgraduate / University Master's
investyourtalentapplication.esteri.it.description: 11th edition of IYT, for the 2026-2027 academic year. Scholarships are for higher-education courses in Italy at participating state/legally recognised institutions, to be completed with a **compulsory internship** at an Italian company or professional association. Applications were open 20 April – 11 May 2026, exclusively online. The call also reserves a quota of Architecture/Design scholarships for applicants from India, Indonesia, Türkiye, Brazil and Ethiopia, and lists 6 participating "Borse Ateneo" universities (Parma, Firenze, Bergamo, Tuscia, Ca' Foscari Venezia, Brescia). Renewals for the 10th edition were due 20 July 2026; renewal for 11th-edition holders is due 20 July 2027.
investyourtalentapplication.esteri.it.benefits: **EUR 10,800 per year**, paid in instalments into an Italian bank account (first instalment EUR 4,800, then EUR 3,000 per quarter). Winners are **exempt from enrolment fees and university contributions** except regional right-to-education tax, stamp duty, accident/civil-liability insurance and health insurance. The scholarship does **not** cover travel or accommodation. Health insurance must be arranged by the holder. Incompatible with any other Italian government or public-institution scholarship (incl. Erasmus+ and regional programmes).

oia-scholarship.nycu.edu.tw.official_source: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (NYCU) — Office of International Affairs
oia-scholarship.nycu.edu.tw.eligibility: new Ph.D. students with outstanding grades who have not received scholarships or grants from the Taiwan government. The surrounding NYCU scholarship guidance also notes that undergraduate recipients must enrol in at least 4 Mandarin courses and graduate students at least 2 during their studies, and that students who extend their study period or reach the maximum scholarship duration may apply for the local student tuition rate if they meet the required academic standard. (source: same)
oia-scholarship.nycu.edu.tw.funding: monthly stipend of **NT$33,000** plus a **tuition waiver for 2 years** (source: same)
oia-scholarship.nycu.edu.tw.description: NYCU's merit award for new doctoral students, allocated on college recommendation and scholarship-committee review rather than open application. The recorded url (https://oia-scholarship.nycu.edu.tw) is NYCU's live international-student scholarship application system but does **not** list this award; at the research date it showed only the "Spring 2027 NYCU New Students Scholarship" (application window 2026-08-10 00:00 to 2026-11-13 11:59, results announced 2026-11-14 00:00, open to foreign students).

unige.ch.official_source: University of Geneva — Faculty of Science (UNIGE)
unige.ch.eligibility: outstanding, highly motivated students who satisfy the admission criteria of their chosen Faculty of Science Master's programme and are selected on the basis of the application file. Each applicant must have completed the UNIGE enrolment procedure (proof = UNIGE card, or the "UNIGE-Candidature: Dépôt de votre dossier" email). Applicants who have already started a Master's at the Faculty of Science cannot apply.
unige.ch.funding: CHF 10,000 – CHF 15,000 per year (grant), with no teaching duties.
unige.ch.benefits: awarded for one year and extended for the regular duration of the chosen Master's programme (three or four semesters) provided the applicant is academically successful at the end of the first semester. Renewal is conditional — it is not automatic.
unige.ch.degree: Master of Science (MSc), 3–4 semesters; disciplines incl. astronomy, biology, chemistry and biochemistry, computer science, mathematics, physics, pharmaceutical sciences, earth and environmental sciences.
unige.ch.description: Fellowship run by the Faculty of Science with support from external partners, awarded on the basis of excellence. A single PDF must contain: national ID/passport scan, CV (max 2 pages), full bachelor transcript with grades, motivation letter, two academic reference letters, plus GRE/TOEFL or other language-test results if available.

id:154.official_source: University of St.Gallen (HSG), in cooperation with the "Monique Dornonville de la Cour - Stiftung"
id:154.eligibility: Enrolled Bachelor students at the University of St.Gallen with outstanding academic performance in the HSG Assessment Year, identified and invited by HSG's Advice Center for Study Funding. Additional selection criteria may apply depending on the funding source; final selection rests with the relevant committees.
id:154.description: HSG Excellence Scholarships for Bachelor students are awarded on the basis of merit. Since 2018 HSG has honoured excellent academic achievement during the HSG assessment year for foreign Bachelor students. This is one of four HSG schemes under the generic term "Excellence Scholarships"; the others are the HSG Best Talents Programme (Master's), the St.Gallen Symposium Excellence Scholarship and the Monique Dornonville de la Cour Foundation Scholarship.
id:154.benefits: The scholarship amount corresponds to the current Bachelor-level tuition fees for a total of 6 semesters. No CHF figure is published on the official page.

id:157.eligibility: National of a CERN Member or Associate Member State (currently **cannot** consider applications from Pakistani, Lithuanian, Latvian, Cypriot, Croatian and Turkish nationals, as the Article II.5 ceiling of the Associate Membership Agreement has been reached). The candidate's university must accept that the CERN research contributes to their doctoral thesis in a CERN field. The candidate has started or is about to start a doctoral programme. Good knowledge of English or French. No age limit stated on the programme page.
id:157.benefits: Coverage by CERN's comprehensive Health Insurance scheme; 30 days paid leave per year plus 2 weeks annual closure of CERN; on-the-job and formal training. Monthly **net allowance of CHF 3 907**, from which the CERN Health Insurance contribution is automatically deducted. Family supplement to the subsistence allowance depending on individual circumstances; travel expenses to Geneva on joining depending on individual circumstances.
id:157.degree: Doctorate (PhD) — contract of 6 months, renewable up to 3 years, spreadable over a maximum of 4 consecutive years so the student can spend time at their university.
id:157.description: A PhD studentship in which the student conducts research at CERN in collaboration with their home university, in science, technology, engineering or mathematics. CERN states that applications from six Associate Member State nationalities are currently not considered.
id:157.application_link: https://careers.cern/jobs/tsc-doct/ (CV in English or French via the CERN online application; academic reference letter and transcript optional; online interview may follow)

id:158.eligibility: National of a CERN Member or Associate Member State (same six nationalities — Pakistani, Lithuanian, Latvian, Cypriot, Croatian, Turkish — currently excluded). PhD held, or to be obtained within six months. **Theoretical/Experimental Physics:** no more than 6 years' research experience after the PhD by the application deadline. **Applied Sciences and Engineering:** no more than 3 years' research experience after the PhD by the application deadline, with up to 6 years exceptionally considered. The candidate must never have held a CERN fellow or graduate contract before.
id:158.benefits: CERN's comprehensive health insurance scheme (covering the fellow, their partner and children) and a contribution to the CERN Pension Fund; 30 days paid leave per year plus 2 weeks during the annual closure of CERN; on-the-job and formal training including language classes; contract of 6 to 24 months, extendable up to 36 months. Monthly **net stipend of CHF 7 004 or CHF 7 425**, depending on degree and years of post-graduation experience. Depending on individual circumstances: an installation grant, family, child and infant allowances, and travel expenses to Geneva on joining CERN.
id:158.description: A postdoctoral fellowship within CERN's broader Graduate Programme for recent PhD graduates in physics and engineering, covering experimental, theoretical and applied science as well as engineering roles. CERN states that vacancies under Experimental Physics, Applied Science and Engineering, and Theoretical Physics each correspond to distinct and separate recruitment processes.

imd.org.official_source: IMD Business School (Institut de Management à Genève), Lausanne
imd.org.eligibility: Common criteria for the merit scholarships — excellence in previous academic and/or professional endeavours including GPA (or equivalent) and GMAT/GRE scores; ability to convince IMD of ambition and potential to use the education to pursue a leadership role; career progression and international exposure; ability to contribute to the overall learning experience of the class; performance during the Assessment Day. Additional, award-specific criteria: MBA5 also requires a 750-word essay; Hilti STEM requires an academic background in STEM and/or passion for STEM; Nestlé gives preference to women from developing countries (employees of Nestlé or its subsidiaries are ineligible); Forté requires a female candidate; BackPack requires a highly talented woman with leadership potential who has faced obstacles that made an MBA feel out of reach (financial constraints, family responsibilities, or past disruptions to her professional path), a commitment to a leadership career, alignment with the BackPack Foundation values of share/dare/care, and no company sponsorship. Bursaries require proven financial need, good academic results, a strong reference letter and steady career progression.
imd.org.benefits: Participation in a high-achieving community of students and mentors; on-the-job and formal training; access to IMD's learning resources. Bursaries are means-tested support; IMD also directs students needing larger amounts to its listed loan providers. **MBA5 CHF 50,000; Hilti STEM CHF 50,000; Nestlé for Women CHF 40,000; Forté for Women CHF 30,000; IMD MBA Merit up to CHF 40,000; BackPack for Women full funding.** All amounts are CHF and are tuition scholarships for the IMD MBA programme; the page states no separate living stipend. **48% of students received a scholarship from IMD** and **more than 50% of IMD's scholarships are awarded to women**.
imd.org.description: IMD's funding page for the MBA programme, covering merit scholarships (some partner-funded), a women-focused scholarship set, a fully funded BackPack award, need-based bursaries and pointers to external funders. Applicants must have applied for and accepted an offer to join the IMD MBA programme.
imd.org.application_link: https://www.imd.org/degree/mba/financing/imd-mba-scholarships (complete the scholarship application in the **Program section of the MBA application form**; the bursary application form is directly in the admissions application)

wipo.int.official_source: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), Geneva — "Working at WIPO" / Fellowship Program
wipo.int.eligibility: At minimum a first-level university degree (e.g. a bachelor's). Depending on the fellowship category there may be additional requirements — minimum professional experience, an advanced degree (Master/PhD), or specific competencies. **No age limit** and **no limit on time since graduation**; former WIPO interns are welcome, but Young Experts Program (YEP) alumni may not apply for any WIPO position within one year of finishing YEP. Ineligible categories per the FAQs: none beyond the above.
wipo.int.benefits: 10 official public holidays per year **plus 2.5 days of annual leave for each full month** of the fellowship; access to WIPO Academy internal training; up to **6 study-leave days per year**; WIPO bears the cost of **UN official-language training** where required by the job duties. **Monthly stipend of CHF 3,000–8,000** depending on academic background and experience relevant to the fellowship. **Contract** up to 12 months, renewable to a total of up to 3 years. **Health insurance:** WIPO pays 100 % of the medical premium for contracts under 12 months, or 75 % for contracts of 12 months or more, and 100 % of the professional accident premium. **Relocation:** WIPO covers travel expenses at the start and end of the fellowship and assists with Swiss visa formalities.
wipo.int.degree: Not degree-bearing. Four fellow categories: (1) Translation fellows (PCT Translation and Terminology Fellowship Program — assistant terminologists, translators, post-editors, translation technologists, technical specialists); (2) Legal case manager fellows (WIPO Domain Name Fellowship Program — young law graduates in internet dispute and trademark law); (3) Visiting and research fellows (Research and Visiting Fellowship Program — economics or statistics background); (4) Other specialised fellows across educational and professional backgrounds.
wipo.int.description: WIPO's Fellowship Program places young professionals at WIPO in Geneva, Switzerland, for 12–36 months, across translation/terminology, domain-name law, research/visiting, and other specialised roles, strengthening IP capacity in member states. A fellowship does not guarantee subsequent employment at WIPO. A fellowship at WIPO does not constitute an exclusive requirement for obtaining a visa.

id:168.official_source: European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA) for the European Commission — Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters
id:168.eligibility: Master's level students from all over the world may apply. Country, duration/credits (12/18/24 months), field of study and year of project selection (2018–2025) are filter facets on the catalogue; there are **no** country-restricted editions.
id:168.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programmes are delivered by consortia of higher-education institutions across multiple countries, with scholarships for outstanding students. The EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue is updated annually and lists the master's programmes currently supported by the EU.
id:168.benefits: Scholarships are awarded per consortium and are not uniform. The official text warns: "While many programs offer Erasmus Mundus scholarships, some do not, as they may be reaching the end of their funding period or have been granted a temporary use of the Erasmus Mundus name after funding." The catalogue lists 218 projects; per-project amounts are not published centrally.

id:173.eligibility: Students who hold a **non-EU/EEA passport** and have applied for a degree programme at the University of Amsterdam may submit an application. Nine faculty/graduate-school schemes are listed (Child Development and Education, Communication Science, Economics and Business, Humanities, Law, Medicine, Psychology, Science, Social Sciences). Continuation depends on satisfactory progress — approximately 80% of credits in any one year.
id:173.degree: Master's (a separate Bachelor's AMS exists at some faculties)
id:173.description: UvA's Amsterdam Merit Scholarship is awarded to outstanding students from outside the EU/EEA to attract them to its international classrooms. It is administered per Faculty/Graduate School rather than centrally, so both the amount and the deadline vary.
id:173.benefits: Varies by faculty; each faculty sets the value and the UvA central office determines the AMS budget each October. Verified examples on UvA's own pages: Letje Lips Amsterdam Merit Scholarship (Graduate School of Humanities) — **EUR 37,500** for 2026-2027 (4 awards); Amsterdam Law School AMS — EUR 25,900 for 2026-2027 (per the faculty page's prior cycle figure) / "to be announced" for 2027-2028.

adelaide.edu.au.eligibility: international student applying to a CRICOS-registered bachelor degree (min 96 units / 2 years equivalent) or a CRICOS-registered master degree (min 72 units / 1.5 years equivalent) at Adelaide University, after credit/RPL; and either an ATAR of 99 (or international equivalent) for undergraduate entry, or a minimum overall GPA of 6.7/7.0 (or comparable) for undergraduate or postgraduate entry, in the qualification used as the basis of admission. Must not be applying to an Excluded Programme, must not be an Australia Awards recipient, and must not hold an International Sponsored Student tuition-fee waiver equal to or greater than the scholarship value.
adelaide.edu.au.funding: 50% tuition-fee reduction, applied as a discount to tuition fees (no cash payment).
adelaide.edu.au.benefits: minimum Program Term GPA of 5.5/7.0 must be maintained in each compulsory Study Period; the scholarship is suspended if the GPA falls below this, and is not applied to the next invoice if the overall GPA falls below it (it resumes if the GPA recovers). Cannot be held concurrently with a sponsor tuition-fee waiver.
adelaide.edu.au.description: High-achiver/academic award of limited places, recognising international students commencing undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degrees who achieved outstanding academic performance in their previous studies. Recipients are notified prior to commencement and the award is applied to the Offer of Admission.

scholarships.uq.edu.au.eligibility: International students who have applied to study **full-time at UQ commencing in 2027** in an eligible programme, have satisfied all conditions of the programme offer, the programme entry rank and English language proficiency requirements, and have achieved a competitive score among the pool of offer holders for their commencement semester. Applicants must **not** have received another UQ scholarship, tuition fee reduction or rebate (the UQ English Language Scholarship excepted) or a full scholarship/sponsorship from another organisation; partial scholarships/sponsorships may be considered.
scholarships.uq.edu.au.funding: **25% reduction in tuition fees per semester, for the duration of the program.** Number awarded "may vary".
scholarships.uq.edu.au.degree: Undergraduate and postgraduate coursework; all study areas
scholarships.uq.edu.au.description: Academic-excellence scholarship for future UQ international students, applied automatically at the point of programme application. The 25% tuition reduction is applied prior to the tuition fees due date each semester.

id:195.eligibility: Must have applied for and met the entry requirements for a graduate research degree at the University of Melbourne, or be currently enrolled in one. Ranked highest by relevant selection panels based on academic results for previous study and research potential; completion of a degree at the same level, relevant professional experience, refereed publications, specialist medical qualifications or original music composition may be taken into account. Quantity: 350.
id:195.degree: Graduate research — Masters by Research; Doctoral
id:195.description: Offered to high-achieving domestic and international students enrolling in a graduate research degree. Domestic research students receive a Research Training Program Scholarship (Fee offset) offer with their course offer; stipend-and-fee-offset offers are made separately but around the same time.
id:195.benefits: "100% fee remission and up to **AUD $138,000**". Components: fee offset for up to 2 years (Masters by Research) or up to 4 years (PhD); fortnightly stipend at **AUD $41,100 per year pro rata (2027 full-time rate)** for up to 2 years (Masters by Research) or up to 3.5 years (PhD), indexed annually, including limited paid sick, parental and partner leave; one-off relocation allowance of **AUD $2,000** (moving from Australian States/Territories other than Victoria) or **AUD $3,000** (moving from outside Australia); Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) Single Membership for international students who require a student visa.

id:196.official_source: The Australian National University — Graduate Research School
id:196.eligibility: Domestic or international student enrolled in (or applying to) an accredited HDR course at ANU, with a minimum **Honours H1 (or H1 equivalent)** in prior studies, who is **not** an Industry PhD candidate receiving a full-time salary. Prospective candidates need no separate application — they are considered via the HDR admission application (selecting "Australia: ANU - Other Scholarship"). Current candidates (typically < 1 year FTE) must submit the ANU "Request for consideration for an HDR scholarship" form.
id:196.funding: **AUD 40,475 per annum** (full-time base stipend rate for 2027), paid fortnightly.
id:196.benefits: Travel and removal allowances for students relocating to Canberra; thesis allowance; dependant-child allowance (**international students only**); paid medical, maternity and parental leave. Payments for 3.5 years (PhD) or 1.5 years (MPhil); 6-month extension available.
id:196.description: ANU runs two annual central scholarship rounds covering the University Research Scholarship, the Research Training Program and other centrally managed scholarships. All eligible HDR applicants are ranked in a merit-based process by ANU Colleges on academic record, research potential, supervisor support, referee reports and English competency. Referee reports must arrive before the scholarship deadline, so applications are advised 2–3 weeks ahead.

qut.edu.au.eligibility: Must meet the academic entry requirements and the minimum English language requirements for the degree programme; be commencing the course for the first time; receive an admission offer into an eligible course. Not eligible if already holding another QUT academic scholarship, or if returning to a prior QUT course of study. Minimum academic standards are published — for postgraduate: completed Australian bachelor's degree or higher → GPA 5.00 on a 7-point scale; 0.50 year or more of incomplete Australian postgraduate study → GPA 5.00/7; completed recognised other bachelor's degree or higher → GPA 5.50/7 or equivalent. Eligible study areas are listed on the page (Architecture and built environment, Arts, Business, Communication, Creative arts, Design, Education, Engineering, Health, Information technology and games, Justice, Law, Mathematics and data science, Project management, Science, Double Degrees, Vertical Double Degrees, International Transfer Programs).
qut.edu.au.benefits: Other benefits may include membership to the QUT College of Excellence. Ongoing scholarship covering **25% of tuition fees per semester** of study, for the full duration of the course provided the ongoing academic requirements of the course are met. No cash component is stated.
qut.edu.au.description: High-achievement award determined solely on academic record; the scholarship offer is issued together with the admissions offer letter, and eligibility reviews can be requested via the admissions offer email.

latrobe.edu.au.eligibility: International students; recipients must maintain full-time enrolment at a La Trobe University campus in Australia and satisfactory academic progress. Award percentage is based on the WAM (weighted average mark) and overall eligibility of the course.
latrobe.edu.au.degree: undergraduate and postgraduate coursework (page states "Future undergraduates, Future postgraduate coursework, International")
latrobe.edu.au.description: Tuition-fee discount for high-achieving international students. The page states STATUS "Open" and gives an opening date of 10 February 2026 and a closing date of 31 December 2027 (Australian DD/MM/YYYY format).
latrobe.edu.au.benefits: Up to **25% reduction in course fees** for the duration of studies — 20% for an Australian Tertiary Admission Rank of 60–74, 25% for 75+.

id:208.official_source: Seoul National University (SNU) Office of Admissions / Office of Global Affairs
id:208.eligibility: Must be **both** (a) a faculty member of a major university in a developing country **without** a Ph.D. degree, **and** (b) a newly admitted student to SNU as a Ph.D. student. Priority is given to faculty from major universities in developing countries in Asia, Africa, South America etc.
id:208.benefits: Round-trip airfare (economy class, booked via the GTS system); Korean language training (evening classes only, during regular semesters); reimbursement of National Health Insurance fee. Full tuition exemption for a maximum of 6 semesters; living expenses **KRW 1,500,000–2,000,000 per month for 3–4 years**.
id:208.description: The SNU President Fellowship Program awards approximately **8 recipients each semester**. Applications are made at the same time as the online admission application to SNU's Office of Admissions (tick the "Application for Scholarship" box), followed by submission of evidential documents to SNU OGA, admission results, an interview, and a decision notice.

id:210.official_source: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) — Office of Admissions
id:210.eligibility: applicants for KAIST International Student Admission; recipients must maintain a GPA above 2.7 out of 4.3 at KAIST after their freshman year to retain the scholarship
id:210.description: KAIST's automatic full-tuition scholarship for admitted international undergraduates. Awardees are entitled on admission, with no separate application and no additional selection stage.
id:210.application_link: https://admission.kaist.ac.kr/intl-undergraduate/application/ApplicationGuide/ApplicationTimeline — there is no separate scholarship process; applicants tick "KAIST scholarship" in the Statement of Financial Resources section of the online admission application
id:210.benefits: full tuition fee — **tuition exemption for 8 semesters**; living expenses **KRW 350,000 per month**; medical health insurance

id:211.official_source: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) — Office of Admissions
id:211.eligibility: open to international applicants to KAIST Master's or Master's–Ph.D. integrated programs, all departments except the Global Digital Innovation – Global IT Technology Program (GDI-GTIP) Track; admission periods Spring/Fall Early and Fall Regular. Applicants already accepted for the KAIST Scholarship are automatically considered, and only highly competitive applicants recommended by the department head are awarded.
id:211.funding: full tuition coverage plus a monthly stipend of **KRW 1,000,000** for 4 regular semesters
id:211.description: The KAIST Global Presidential Scholarship is the top tier of KAIST's graduate scholarship scheme, awarded automatically to a small number of department-recommended admitted students.

uic.yonsei.ac.kr.eligibility: newly admitted international students to UIC. All UIC international applicants are automatically considered as scholarship candidates; recipients are selected from admitted applicants according to their academic credentials, the offer letter is enclosed in the admission packet and sent individually, and recipients must maintain a certain GPA each semester to remain eligible. The International Students Track requires a non-Korean applicant with non-Korean parents; an applicant with dual Korean citizenship is not eligible. From the AY 2027 intake, proof of English proficiency is mandatory. (sources: https://uic.yonsei.ac.kr/main/admission.php?mid=m04_03_02 and .../mid=m04_02_02)
uic.yonsei.ac.kr.description: UIC's Admissions Scholarship is an automatic-consideration award covering full tuition for four years for newly admitted international undergraduates, decided on academic credentials at the point of admission. UIC also runs merit-based and need-based scholarships (full, half or one-third of per-semester tuition) restricted to currently enrolled students, plus occasional other opportunities.
uic.yonsei.ac.kr.application_link: https://enter.jinhakapply.com/Notice/1108082/A (direct online application) or the Common Application; application fee KRW 150,000 (approx. USD 150) or USD 150, and UIC states it does not offer or accept a fee waiver
uic.yonsei.ac.kr.benefits: **full tuition for 4 years.** For context, UIC's 2026 international-student tuition is KRW 8,202,000 per semester (KRW 8,416,000 for the first semester), plus KRW 56,000 in miscellaneous fees, i.e. KRW 8,258,000 per semester. (source: https://uic.yonsei.ac.kr/main/admission.php?mid=m04_03_02)

aai-salzburg.at.official_source: Afro-Asian Institute Salzburg (AAI), Archdiocese of Salzburg
aai-salzburg.at.eligibility: Citizenship of a country in the Global South (Africa, Asia, Near and Middle East, Oceania, Caribbean, Latin America); admission to a regular Master's or PhD programme at a public university or university of applied sciences in Salzburg (University of Salzburg, UAS Salzburg, Mozarteum); for PhD candidates a confirmation of supervision; maximum age at application — 30 (35 for mothers) for Master's, 35 (40 for mothers) for doctoral; valid "student" residence permit or student visa; financial need; good academic progress; interest in and commitment to sustainable development/social justice. No awards for private universities, postgraduate certificate/Lehrgang programmes, blended/distance learning without compulsory attendance in Austria, non-degree ("außerordentliche") students, short visits or exchange programmes. Joint Master's only by prior arrangement.
aai-salzburg.at.funding: **EUR 500 per month** partial scholarship during the semester (October through June).
aai-salzburg.at.benefits: Personal mentoring; educational programme of workshops, field trips and social activities; awareness-raising on global challenges; diverse opportunities for participation; global alumni network.
aai-salzburg.at.description: One World Scholarship for students from the Global South already studying in Salzburg. Selection is multi-stage (online form → formal criteria check → documents → content assessment → online interview → Grants Committee decision) and applicants must already be enrolled in Austria or hold at least an admission to a regular degree programme.

id:219.official_source: Universität Innsbruck — Vice-Rectorate for Research, Project Service Office (Research Funding and Mentoring)
id:219.eligibility: All doctoral students (including members of doctoral colleges) **enrolled as regular students at the University of Innsbruck and registered for continuation**; the dissertation must be registered. Applicants must show evidence of excellent academic success (excellent GPA plus normal duration of study — minimum study duration plus 2 tolerance semesters per study/section; any excess must be justified in the CV) or scientific achievements. A maximum of two resubmissions is possible. Priority is given to applicants involved in the University's main research areas and/or project proposals, and at least 50% of the available funding is to be awarded to women. No employment at the University of Innsbruck is permitted during the scholarship; employment elsewhere of more than 15 hours per week cancels the grant. Applicants not who completed their undergraduate studies at UIBK must additionally supply their graduation certificate and all diploma/bachelor's/master's certificates.
id:219.benefits: Any paper published as part of the funded study programme — including the dissertation — must acknowledge the scholarship granted by the University of Innsbruck, Vice-Rectorate for Research, and name the University of Innsbruck in the affiliation. UIBK points scholars to external funders for continuation (Austrian Academy of Sciences DOC/DOC team, TNF, third-party funded employment such as FWF, EU, FFG). **EUR 1 120 per month**, for a maximum of 24 months, with an interim review after 6 months (grant fixed 6 months at a time) and up to two interruptions, each no longer than 6 months. Conceived as start-up/interim/bridge/final funding for doctoral students. Paid exclusively by SEPA transfer.
id:219.description: University of Innsbruck doctoral scholarship supporting young academics on the way to an academic career, funded as a fixed-term start-up/bridge grant rather than as a full PhD salary. Required documents: a description of the planned dissertation project (8–12 pages), a half-page layperson-readable abstract in German, a recommendation letter from the dissertation supervisor, CV and publication list.

id:231.official_source: Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst (DAAD) — German Academic Exchange Service
id:231.eligibility: You can apply if you have gained a first university degree in Architecture, Interior Design, Monument Conservation and Building in Existing Contexts/Reconditioning of Old Buildings, Urban Design/Urban Development, Landscape Architecture or Landscape Planning at the latest by the time you commence your scholarship-supported study programme. Last relevant university degree should not date back more than 6 years at the application deadline; not eligible if resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline.
id:231.benefits: monthly rent subsidy; monthly family allowance; disability/chronic-illness cost subsidy (case by case); Green Mobility Top Up or carbon-offset reimbursement for air travel; German language course (2/4/6 months) if required €992 per month; travel allowance (upon application only); one-off study allowance; payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance
id:231.degree: Master's/postgraduate degree leading to a final qualification, or a complementary course without a degree, at a state or state-recognised German university of your choice
id:231.description: Funding period 10–24 months depending on the chosen programme for degree studies; start usually 1 October of the following year, or earlier if a German language course is taken first. Complementary studies without a degree: one academic year. The programme funds projects in the area of Design/Projects.

id:232.official_source: Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst (DAAD) — German Academic Exchange Service
id:232.eligibility: You can apply if you have gained a first university degree in the field of arts. University degree should not date back more than 6 years at the application deadline; not eligible if resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline.
id:232.benefits: monthly rent subsidy; monthly family allowance; disability/chronic-illness cost subsidy (case by case); Green Mobility Top Up or carbon-offset reimbursement for air travel €992 per month; travel allowance (upon application only); one-off study allowance; payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance
id:232.degree: Master's/postgraduate course leading to a final qualification at a state or state-recognised German university of your choice, **or** a complementary course without degree (study year in Germany as part of a home-university programme, or an independent project/complementary course with a professor in Germany)
id:232.description: Degree studies 10–24 months depending on programme; complementary studies without degree one academic year (usually 12 months). Start usually 1 October of the following year, or earlier if a German language course is taken first. A connection to a university in the fields of art in Germany is mandatory and must be verified with a confirmation of supervision. Selection can take up to seven months from submission to notification.

id:233.official_source: Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst (DAAD) — German Academic Exchange Service
id:233.eligibility: The programme is aimed at graduates from the field of Music. Eligible if you will have obtained a first degree in music by the time the scholarship begins, or you have exhausted all training opportunities for your instrument or subject in your home country where no degree is offered. University degree should not date back more than 6 years at the application deadline; not resident in Germany for more than 15 months prior to the deadline.
id:233.benefits: monthly rent subsidy; monthly family allowance; disability/chronic-illness cost subsidy (case by case); Green Mobility Top Up or carbon-offset reimbursement for air travel €992 per month; travel allowance (upon application only); one-off study allowance; payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance
id:233.degree: degree studies (Master's, Konzertexamen, Meisterklasse) at a Staatliche Musikhochschule in Germany of your choice, **or** advanced studies without a degree (2 semesters / 12 months)
id:233.description: Degree-study funding period is 2–4 semesters depending on the standard period of study (10 months up to a maximum of 24 months); advanced studies without a degree are 2 semesters (12 months), extendable on application. A connection to a college of music in Germany is mandatory and must be proven by a written confirmation of supervision.

id:234.official_source: Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst (DAAD) — German Academic Exchange Service
id:234.eligibility: You can apply if you have gained a first university degree in the field of the Performing Arts at the latest by the time you commence your scholarship-supported study programme. University degree should not date back more than 6 years at the application deadline; not eligible if resident in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline.
id:234.benefits: monthly rent subsidy; monthly family allowance; disability/chronic-illness cost subsidy (case by case); Green Mobility Top Up or carbon-offset reimbursement for air travel €992 per month; travel allowance (upon application only); one-off study allowance; payments towards health, accident and personal liability insurance
id:234.degree: Master's/postgraduate course leading to a final qualification at a state or state-recognised German university of your choice, **or** a complementary course without degree (study year in Germany or an independent project/complementary course with a professor in Germany)
id:234.description: Degree studies 10–24 months depending on the chosen programme; complementary studies without a degree one academic year (usually 12 months). Start usually 1 October of the following year, or earlier if a German language course is taken first. A connection to a university in the performing arts in Germany is mandatory and must be verified with a confirmation of supervision. Selection can take up to seven months from submission to notification.
id:234.application_link: https://www2.daad.de/deutschland/stipendium/datenbank/en/21148-scholarship-database/?detail=50109971 — online via the DAAD portal (page also states the application runs through the DAAD Portal between 4 November and 4 December in the relevant cycle)

boell.de.official_source: Heinrich Böll Foundation (Heinrich-Böll-Stiftung e.V.), Scholarship Department / Studienwerk — official programme name "**Tailwind for Talents**"
boell.de.eligibility: Students — international students who have completed their first degree abroad can apply prior to starting a Master's programme in Germany; priority is given to applicants from DAC countries who have not yet taken up residence in Germany at the time of application. PhD students — international PhD students who completed their graduate degree abroad may apply for a PhD programme in Germany; priority to DAC-country nationals not yet resident in Germany.
boell.de.benefits: academic experiential learning activities, expert encounters, industrial visits, international conference participation and Korean-language-class-style pre-departure orientations are listed for KOICA (not applicable here) — for Böll see the guidance pages "Financial support", "Applying for a scholarship", "Getting started as (Under)Graduate", "Promotion Funding" at https://www.boell.de/en/scholarships **Master's**: base scholarship €992/month + health insurance allowance up to €100/month + fixed fringe benefits €38/month. **PhD**: base scholarship €1,500/month + health insurance up to €200/month + fixed fringe benefits €38/month. Both may add: reimbursement of tuition fees in Germany of up to €10,000/year; tuition fees for German language courses; family allowance and child allowances (per child). Funded by the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) and the Federal Foreign Office (AA). Additional income must be offset against the scholarship payment.
boell.de.description: In its effort to foster equal opportunities and equitable access to education, the Heinrich Böll Foundation supports graduate students and PhD students from DAC countries who intend to pursue a Master's degree or PhD in Germany. Contact: studienwerk@boell.de

id:240.eligibility: privately-financed international student planning to enrol **full-time** using pre-arrival admission (selection and admission granted without coming to Japan first); three reservation categories — (1) graduate level, (2) EJU exam (schools on JASSO's registered pre-arrival list; JASSO used the list as of 1 October 2025 for spring enrolment and 1 April 2026 for September/October enrolment), (3) English courses (undergraduate courses/associate degrees taught only in English that offer pre-arrival admission). "Full-time student" excludes research students, trainees, non-degree, advanced-course, special-course, auditing and special students.
id:240.funding: monthly stipend of **JPY 48,000** (the page notes the amount may change from one academic year to another)
id:240.benefits: 12 months (April enrolment to the following March) or 6 months (September/October enrolment, from October to the following March)
id:240.description: Reservation track of the JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately-Financed International Students, for students who have already secured pre-arrival admission to a Japanese institution. The procedure must be completed through the enrolling school.

id:244.official_source: Tsinghua University — Graduate Admissions for International Students (the Chinese Government Scholarship itself is administered by the Chinese Scholarship Council / CSC)
id:244.description: Category B Chinese Government Scholarship places at Tsinghua. Students cannot apply directly: they must first obtain Tsinghua pre-admission and a recommendation from the admitting school/department, then complete the separate CSC online application.
id:244.application_link: https://yzbm.tsinghua.edu.cn/intlLogin (Tsinghua pre-admission application, then the CSC Online Application System)
id:244.benefits: Full CGS covers tuition fees, free university dormitory or accommodation subsidy, stipend, and comprehensive medical insurance. A Partial CGS includes one or some items from the Full CGS coverage. No monetary amounts are published on this page. (source: same)

id:251.official_source: Trinity College Dublin, The University of Dublin
id:251.eligibility: applicants must have a non-EU fee status with tuition billed at a non-EU rate and must already hold a course offer for a full-time undergraduate degree at Trinity. Students from China are not eligible and are directed to the Claddagh Undergraduate Scholarship instead. (source: same)
id:251.description: Trinity's undergraduate Global Excellence Scholarship, one of the two levels of a single Global Excellence scheme. Early application is advised; applications are assessed and awarded on a rolling basis, and awardees must fully accept their course offer to receive the award. Selection is based on academic achievement and the applicant's potential to contribute to the Trinity community.
id:251.application_link: https://eu.surveymonkey.com/r/tges (external application form linked from the recorded page)
id:251.benefits: "Scholarships range in value between **€2,000 and €5,000** depending on the region", applied as a reduction to the year-one tuition fees of a full-time undergraduate programme. (source: same)

id:252.official_source: Trinity College Dublin, The University of Dublin
id:252.eligibility: applicants must have a non-EU fee status with tuition billed at a non-EU rate and must already hold a course offer for a full-time postgraduate taught programme at Trinity. Students from China are not eligible and are directed to the Claddagh Postgraduate Scholarship instead. (source: same)
id:252.description: Trinity's postgraduate Global Excellence Scholarship, the taught-postgraduate level of the same Global Excellence scheme as the undergraduate award. Applications are assessed and awarded on a rolling basis; awardees must fully accept their course offer. Selection is based on academic achievement and potential to contribute to the Trinity community.
id:252.application_link: https://eu.surveymonkey.com/r/tges (external application form linked from the recorded page)
id:252.benefits: "Scholarships range in value between **€2,000 and €5,000** depending on the region", applied as a one-time reduction to the tuition fees of a full-time postgraduate taught programme. (source: same)

id:260.official_source: Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington
id:260.eligibility: International students paying full international fees; intending a Master's degree of 120, 180 or 240 points or a Postgraduate Diploma of 120 points at VUW; holder of an unconditional or conditional Offer of Place; new to the programme. Not eligible: returning students (unless completing VUW's EAP or a VUW Bachelor's/Bachelor with Honours); Study Abroad, Exchange or Twinning students; students with credit transfer/advanced standing; students sponsored by their home government or the New Zealand Government; Australian or New Zealand citizens, permanent residents, resident-visa holders or diplomatic-visa holders with domestic status.
id:260.degree: Master's by thesis; Master's by coursework; Postgraduate Diploma
id:260.description: Partial fee-based scholarship for new international students entering a full-time Master's or Postgraduate Diploma, awarded automatically on the basis of the programme application.
id:260.benefits: **NZ$10,000** for one year of study, credited to tuition fees only and applied directly against fees upfront. Awarded once per student.

id:263.eligibility: talented **non-EU/non-EEA** students liable to pay tuition fees at Aalto. Applicants who are liable to pay tuition fees only; those not liable (EU/EEA citizens) are not eligible. Merit-based, competitive, awarded to the highest-achieving applicants against the programme's own evaluation criteria. A very limited number of scholarships exist and some programmes award none.
id:263.description: Awarded for the target time of the degree programme — three years of full-time study for a bachelor's, two years for a master's — and the scholarship terms must be accepted by a stated deadline. Study progress is checked annually to confirm the holder is on track. Applicants admitted from the waiting list are not eligible for a scholarship. The same official page also lists separate named awards: the **Pekka Mattila scholarship** (a EUR 3,000 relocation grant for Master's students in Business, Marketing and International Management), a **25 % tuition-fee discount** for scholarship holders funded by FUNED (Mexico) or COLFUTURO (Colombia), and **Aalto Foundation scholarships**. International joint/double-degree programmes follow their own tuition-fee and scholarship regulations.
id:263.benefits: a **tuition-fee waiver covering the full tuition fee**. Bachelor's: EUR 12,000 per academic year for Business, Economics and Technology; EUR 15,000 for Art, Design and Architecture. Master's: EUR 15,000 (Business), EUR 17,000 (Technology and Engineering), EUR 17,000 (multidisciplinary), EUR 20,000 (Art, Design and Architecture), per academic year. Living costs are **not** covered — Aalto students must be able to fund at least EUR 800 per month themselves.
