masters.au.dk.eligibility: Applicants who are liable to pay tuition fees (EU/EEA/Swiss students cannot apply). Scholarships can only be awarded to tuition-fee-liable applicants. Priority is given to applicants with excellent academic qualifications; typically only one or two scholarships are offered per Master's programme, and at some faculties the focus is on selected degree programmes or applicants from specific countries. Late offers may still be made up to 1 April (summer) / 1 November (winter).
masters.au.dk.description: State-financed Danish scholarships automatically assessed alongside the admission application for tuition-fee-paying non-EU/EEA master's applicants; the type of award varies by faculty.
masters.au.dk.benefits: **Faculty-dependent, and no amount is published.** Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS: full tuition fee waiver **plus** a monthly grant towards living expenses. Faculty of Natural Sciences and Faculty of Technical Sciences: **tuition fee waiver only** (no living grant). Because a tuition waiver alone is not enough for a Danish residence permit, students with a waiver only must demonstrate sufficient funds themselves.

sdu.dk.eligibility: non-EU/EEA citizens only, and only for programmes offered on the Sønderborg and Vejle campuses. EU/EEA full-degree and exchange students pay no tuition fee; non-EU/EEA full-degree students pay tuition + a EUR application deposit fee plus residence-permit fees.
sdu.dk.benefits: State Education Grant (SU) is described separately (normally requires Danish citizenship, though foreign citizens can apply for equal status under specific criteria, see www.su.dk). SDU explicitly states it does **not** provide emergency financial assistance. "SDU offers a **very limited number of scholarships** for non EU/EEA citizens. Scholarships can only be awarded for programmes offered on our campuses in Sønderborg and Vejle." The page publishes no amount or percentage.
sdu.dk.description: Fees-and-funding overview page for SDU international students. The only university-administered scholarship SDU advertises is a very limited number of non-EU/EEA awards tied to its Sønderborg and Vejle campuses.

id:274.eligibility: minimum overall GPA of "A" on the ECTS scale (or equivalent top-level international grade); Norwegian or international citizenship (international citizens who completed a bachelor's degree in Norway count as residents of Norway); admitted to year 1 of a master's programme at campus Oslo or campus Bergen, excluding the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing; only candidates seeking their first master's degree. 3rd-year Sivøk students may apply by email in spring of their 3rd year. Scholars must maintain 30 ECTS per semester and a cumulative "B" on the BI ECTS scale, and act as "BI Ambassadors".
id:274.description: Merit-based (not need-based) scholarship awarded to admitted master's applicants with superior academic records at BI's Oslo or Bergen campuses. All applicants, including those not selected, are informed of the decision by the end of April; scholarship decisions are final and cannot be appealed.
id:274.application_link: https://apply.bi.no/applicant  (scholarship section of the online admission application; scholarship applications are not accepted by email except 3rd-year Sivøk)
id:274.benefits: full tuition fees each semester for up to two years. Norwegian/international applicants resident in Norway and Sivøk applicants: tuition only. International applicants: tuition for up to two years **plus a living-expense stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester**.

id:275.eligibility: international citizenship and **not** resident of Norway; minimum overall GPA of 4.0 on the ECTS scale (international grades converted by BI); admitted to a Master of Science programme at campus Bergen; only candidates seeking their first master's degree; candidates who completed a bachelor's degree in Norway are treated as domestic and are not eligible. Applicants who apply for the BI Presidential Scholarship are also considered for this one with no separate letter.
id:275.description: Merit-based tuition-fee scholarship for strong international applicants to any MSc programme at BI's Bergen campus. Applicants must submit CV plus a one-page scholarship letter in a single PDF in the 'Scholarship' section of the admission application; nothing submitted after the admission application is considered.
id:275.benefits: full tuition fees for up to two years if academic progression requirements are met. No living stipend is stated on this page.

id:276.eligibility: minimum 33 IB points (final or predicted); Norwegian or international citizenship; an offer of admission to one of BI's Bachelor of Business Administration, Bachelor of Data Science for Business, or Bachelor of Digital Business programmes; first bachelor's degree only. Final-year high-school students must submit final transcripts in June/July, no later than the end of the first week of July.
id:276.description: IB-specific merit scholarship for top-scoring International Baccalaureate students. Bachelor's scholarships are awarded in two rounds — end of April (international applicants) and July (Norwegian residents / internationals in Norwegian high schools).
id:276.benefits: 100 % of tuition fees for up to three years, conditional on academic progression (30 ECTS per semester; minimum cumulative "B" on the BI ECTS scale).

id:277.eligibility: preference for candidates currently enrolled at or recently graduated from a **GBSN member school in Africa**, or citizens of an African country who took part in a GMAC Study in Europe event in Africa; international citizenship and not resident of Norway; must submit strong GMAT or GRE scores required for admission; minimum overall GPA 4.0 on the ECTS scale; admitted to year 1 of an MSc at campus Oslo or Bergen, excluding the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing; first master's degree only.
id:277.description: Two merit MSc scholarships BI offers as a member of the Global Business School Network and of GMAC's Study in Europe Initiative, aimed specifically at candidates from Africa. Applicants identify their GBSN school or their GMAC event (with date and place) in the scholarship letter.
id:277.benefits: full tuition fees for up to two years **plus a living-expense stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester**. BI offers two such MSc scholarships.

kuleuven.be.official_source: KU Leuven (funded by the KU Leuven International Scholarship Fund)
kuleuven.be.eligibility: all nationalities; all master's and advanced master's programmes at KU Leuven (preparatory, bridging and distance-learning programmes excluded); high academic performance/GPA; previous degree(s) obtained at an institution **outside Flanders**; English: Online TOEFL iBT ≥94, IELTS ≥7.0 or Cambridge CPE C2 (exempt if previously completed an English-taught programme in Australia, English-speaking Canada, Ireland, NZ, UK or US); must not already be enrolled at a Flemish HEI (exception: international students enrolled in a preparatory programme in spring 2026 to start in September 2026); **may not be combined with any other scholarship**
kuleuven.be.benefits: duration of one academic year for a 60 ECTS master's programme and two academic years for a 120 ECTS master's programme full tuition-fee waiver (holders pay only an annual administration fee of circa €140) + €13,200 per academic year, for a maximum of two academic years; 1 scholarship available in 2026-2027
kuleuven.be.description: A single application automatically also puts the candidate forward for the Master Mind Scholarship, KU Leuven ASEAN Scholarship, KU Leuven Scholarship for Africa and KU Leuven Scholarship for Central and South America (subject to nationality conditions). Nomination notifications by 10 March 2026; a one-minute motivational video is required by 18 March 2026; results at the end of March/beginning of April 2026.
kuleuven.be.application_link: https://www.kuleuven.be/english/apply (Step 1, with the KU Leuven Scholarships & Master Mind Candidacy Form as annexe) then https://www.kuleuven.be/scholarships/year/2026-2027/registration (Step 2)

id:289.official_source: Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA) — joint initiative with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Polish development aid)
id:289.eligibility: citizens of the 36 countries covered by Polish Aid from Eastern Europe, Asia, Africa and Latin America (full list in the call announcement); must be admitted to a Polish HEI supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that has a framework agreement with NAWA; B2 language certificate; max 1 application
id:289.funding: monthly scholarship of PLN 2,500 + exemption from tuition fees at public universities + travel allowance of PLN 2,500
id:289.benefits: NAWA-funded preparatory Polish course (Polish track); Polish language and culture course (English track); studies in Polish or English
id:289.description: Offers scholarships for full-time second-cycle studies at universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education, in order to support the socio-economic development of developing countries. Applications are also capped at 300 per country group (200 in group no. 4).

id:290.official_source: Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange (NAWA)
id:290.eligibility: citizens of the listed Programme countries (Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Chile, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Spain, Hong Kong, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Macau, Malta, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, South Korea, Romania, Singapore, Slovakia, Slovenia, Switzerland, Sweden, Taiwan, UK, USA, Uruguay) or residents of Hong Kong/Macau/Taiwan; not Polish citizens and must not have applied for Polish citizenship; first-cycle degree obtained in a Programme country no earlier than 2024 (or final-year student graduating by 15 July 2026); planning full-time second-cycle studies in 2026/27; no prior NAWA Director's scholarship for second-cycle studies; B2 Polish or B2 English
id:290.description: Encourages young people from developed countries to study at Polish academic HEIs that have concluded a framework agreement with NAWA. NAWA does not mediate admission — applicants apply to the university independently.
id:290.benefits: scholarship of the Director of NAWA — PLN 2,000.00 per month from 1 January 2026 (per NAWA Announcement No. 47/2025 of 17 December 2025, which amends Call 13/2025 of the PMFC programme) + tuition-free education at public higher education institutions

novasbe.unl.pt.official_source: NOVA School of Business and Economics (Nova SBE), Carcavelos, Portugal
novasbe.unl.pt.eligibility: "All candidates can apply for this scholarship, regardless of their country of origin." Interest must be shown **in the Master's application form**; applications are open for the Fall intake and cannot be considered after the Master's application has been submitted. To maintain the award, students must check the merit criteria at the end of their first year. Candidates must monitor their own email (including spam/trash). Only one Nova SBE scholarship is awarded per applicant.
novasbe.unl.pt.description: Nova SBE's Master's scholarship portfolio covers academic merit and social mobility. Alongside the Merit Scholarship the same page lists the Nova SBE Social Mobility Scholarship, the Nova SBE Continuity Scholarship, the Nova SBE Women in Finance Scholarship (20 % or 50 % of tuition, International Master's in Finance, cannot be combined with the Merit Scholarship), the Accenture Scholarship (100 % of tuition, applications 13 Nov 2025 – 23 Mar 2026 for the Fall intake) and the André Sousa Bessa Scholarship, plus the separate Direção Geral do Ensino Superior (DGES) Scholarship, whose 2026/27 applications opened on 14 August.
novasbe.unl.pt.application_link: https://www.novasbe.unl.pt/en/programs/apply/masters/eligibility  (the scholarship section of the Master's application form — there is no separate scholarship application portal)
novasbe.unl.pt.benefits: **Nova SBE Merit Scholarship — 20 % or 50 % of the tuition-fee value** of the Master's programme. When combined with other Nova SBE scholarships, funding cannot exceed 70 % of total Master's tuition, except where the funding is entirely a 100 % social-mobility scholarship. The prize does not cover the application fee, the first tuition instalment paid as an enrolment fee, the CEMS programme, the Double Degree programme, additional semesters, exchange programmes or Executive Master's programmes.

id:317.official_source: Tsinghua University — Graduate Admissions for International Students (the scholarship is offered by Bai Xian Asia Institute)
id:317.eligibility: non-Chinese citizens from Asia who meet the requirements for admission to Tsinghua's 2026 international master's programs; academic excellence, leadership potential, integrity and character, a keen interest in international and intercultural understanding, compassion and commitment to service, and appreciation of BXAI's mission; good command of English and presentation skills; not in receipt of other Tsinghua scholarships. (source: https://yz.tsinghua.edu.cn/en/info/1027/1477.htm)
id:317.description: The Asian Future Leaders Scholarship Program, offered by Bai Xian Asia Institute, funds prospective full-time international students from Asia to pursue a Tsinghua master's in AY 2026-2027. After the departmental recommendation list reaches the University by 2026-03-23, Tsinghua nominates to BXAI by end of April 2026 and candidates are informed by end of May 2026.
id:317.application_link: https://yzbm.tsinghua.edu.cn/intlLogin (Tsinghua master's application, September 2025 to February 2026), then scholarship materials are emailed to the target department/school
id:317.benefits: tuition fees plus a living allowance covering accommodation, books or other materials, for one or two years. No monetary amount is published. (source: same)

bs.china-embassy.gov.cn.official_source: Embassy of the People's Republic of China in The Bahamas (Nassau), Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC
bs.china-embassy.gov.cn.eligibility: **Bahamian citizens.** Scholarships are aimed at undergraduate, master's, doctoral and advanced general studies at Chinese universities. Applicants may choose courses taught in Chinese or in English; universities with the scholarship programme generally provide a 1-year Chinese language course for applicants needing it. Applications are submitted via the Chinese Government Scholarship information system (Study in China / campuschina.org) with embassy review and recommendation. The Bahamas Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Bahamas-China Friendship Association also publish relevant information. Contact: chinaemb_bs@mfa.gov.cn
bs.china-embassy.gov.cn.funding: The Chinese Government Scholarship covers **tuition, accommodation, living expenses and international air tickets**.
bs.china-embassy.gov.cn.degree: Undergraduate, Master's, Doctorate and advanced general studies
bs.china-embassy.gov.cn.description: Chinese Government Scholarships awarded annually to Bahamians for study at Chinese universities, in Chinese- or English-medium programmes, with the embassy assisting university review and making recommendations. The same embassy notice also covers the **Chinese MOFCOM Scholarship** for Master's and PhD degrees, hosted by universities including Peking University and Tsinghua University and covering round-trip international airfare, tuition, accommodation and a living stipend; that programme usually starts each September for 1–2 years, with applications accepted between April and early June and a **deadline of 6 June Beijing time**.
bs.china-embassy.gov.cn.application_link: http://bs.china-embassy.gov.cn/eng/ (embassy announcements) — official application portal is www.campuschina.org

international.au.dk.official_source: Aarhus University (administering **Danish state** funding for non-EU/EEA students). Note: "Our scholarships are financed by the Danish state. Aarhus University does not have its own scholarship funds, but rely solely on funding from the Danish state for this purpose."
international.au.dk.eligibility: Applicants liable to pay tuition fees (i.e. non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens without a fee-exempt residence permit). **No separate application** — the admission application is automatically assessed with a view to a scholarship. EU/EEA/Swiss students cannot apply for scholarships at AU. Priority is given to applicants with excellent academic qualifications; typically only one or two scholarships are offered per Master's programme. At some faculties strategic focus is placed on selected degree programmes or applicants from specific countries. Selection offers come with the letter of admission and carry a very short acceptance deadline.
international.au.dk.description: Aarhus University offers a limited number of Danish state scholarships to the most talented applicants from outside Europe who are liable to pay tuition fees. Students who are offered a waiver only are not notified by the university and are required to pay fees if no waiver offer arrives by 1 April / 1 November.
international.au.dk.benefits: Content varies by faculty — a full or partial tuition waiver, in some cases including a monthly grant toward living expenses, typically but not always for the duration of the Master's. Stated types: Faculty of Arts and Aarhus BSS = tuition fee waiver + monthly living-expense grant; Faculty of Natural Sciences and Faculty of Technical Sciences = tuition fee waiver only. Where only a waiver is offered, the student must still show sufficient funds for the residence permit (SIRI self-support requirement). Waiver awards for Natural/Technical Sciences may also be made during March, up to the acceptance deadline of 1 April (summer) / 1 November (winter).

en.aau.dk.official_source: Aalborg University (AAU) — financed by the Danish Government, awarded by Aalborg University
en.aau.dk.eligibility: Each September intake AAU grants a limited number of scholarships to individually selected applicants from non-EU/EEA countries based on strategic considerations and academic qualifications; **approximately 15 each year**. AAU advises not to rely on receiving a scholarship. AAU's FAQ states it is not possible to apply for a scholarship from AAU separately.
en.aau.dk.description: Scholarship decisions are communicated to all applicants **by the beginning of July at the latest** for the September intake. AAU does not offer tuition waivers or scholarships for bachelor's programmes.
en.aau.dk.application_link: https://www.en.aau.dk/education/apply (automatic consideration within the master's application)
en.aau.dk.benefits: A scholarship consists of a **tuition fee waiver plus a monthly stipend** aimed at covering living expenses during the four semesters of the master's programme. Stipend rate for new students in 2026: **11,225 DKK / 1,503 EUR per month** (tax may apply). Stipend is paid for four semesters; no further stipend beyond the first two years.

id:333.official_source: University of Helsinki (RESDOC — Resilient and Just Systems Doctoral Project; an international doctoral training project at the University of Helsinki in Finland)
id:333.funding: "a fully funded doctoral degree at the University of Helsinki in Finland" — no salary figure is published on this page.
id:333.description: RESDOC brings together interdisciplinary, cross-sectoral research on climate change, biodiversity loss and infectious diseases, organised around four themes: infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance; biodiversity and nature's resilience; sustainable food and water systems; and just socio-ecological transition. The doctoral period is 2027–2031.

id:334.official_source: University of Helsinki — University of Helsinki Doctoral School (UHDS)
id:334.description: UHDS provides annual funding for doctoral researcher positions across all of the University's doctoral programmes, with one application round per year. Detailed general and programme-specific instructions are published in the University's Studies Service; the list of awarded positions is published on the same page (marked "as of 11.12.2025, subject to change").
id:334.benefits: salaried full-time employment. Positions are designated as full-time work and the aim is that the doctoral degree is completed within four years. No salary amount is published on this page.

id:343.eligibility: Pursuing a doctoral degree in Information and Communications Technologies (ICT) or in areas supporting the development of ICT, either at a Finnish university or (for Finnish applicants) at a university abroad. Applicant should have a record of fast-paced, high-quality doctoral studies and one or more accepted publications intended for the dissertation. Requires a commitment statement from the principal supervisor (a professor, docent or senior scientist at the degree-granting university), submitted through the electronic application tool.
id:343.funding: Up to EUR 7,500. Can be granted only once to the same individual.
id:343.description: Encourages efficient, fast-progressing doctoral studies and research in ICT. Application submission opened 3 August 2026. Recipients are published in December 2026 and scholarships are paid directly to grantees by end of December 2026.

id:344.eligibility: Project must be carried out in a Finnish university and be led by a tenured associate or full professor acting as Principal Investigator. One application per professor per call. A proposed financial plan with a detailed breakdown (salary, overhead, other expenses) is required. Research security and ethics aspects must be comprehensively explained.
id:344.degree: Doctoral or postdoctoral researcher (the grant finances hiring the researcher, not the researcher themself)
id:344.description: Supports innovative, pioneering ICT research projects that can open genuinely new frontiers. Grant decisions are scheduled for late October 2026; funded projects may begin in early 2027 and must conclude no later than August 2028. Successful projects may reapply for an extension via the next year's process.

southafrica-france-scholarships.com.official_source: French Embassy in South Africa — France-South Africa Scholarship Programme
southafrica-france-scholarships.com.eligibility: citizenship of South Africa, Lesotho or Malawi; dual French citizens are not eligible; a minimum average of 60% in the most recently completed degree. Master's applicants must plan to enrol in a French higher education institution (admission is not required at the time of application); PhD applicants must plan to pursue a PhD in France and have identified a prospective supervisor or research laboratory. Applicants may list a maximum of three study programmes in order of preference, and must supply links to programme pages, application dates and tuition fees. Proof of acceptance must be provided between February and July 2027. Applications must include a cover letter, copies of previous degree certificates, university transcripts covering at least three years, academic and/or professional recommendations and French language proficiency certificates (TCF, DELF, DALF etc.).
southafrica-france-scholarships.com.benefits: laureates attend intensive online French courses delivered through the Alliances Françaises network from February to July 2027; shortlisted candidates may be offered an internship with a French company or organisation in South Africa; depending on profile, placement is available in business, administration or the public sector. a monthly living allowance of **€900 for Master's students and €1,850 for PhD students**, subject to reassessment; **one return flight ticket** between the recipient's country of residence and France; eligibility to apply for additional housing support from the French Family Allowance Fund (CAF) of approximately **€150 per month** depending on individual circumstances. The award also carries France Excellence scholarship-holder status: social security coverage and health insurance, priority access to student housing, exemption from visa fees, support services from Campus France Paris, exemption from the Student and Campus Life Contribution (CVEC), and conditional exemption from registration fees for programmes at public universities applying the standard national non-EU tuition rate. **Tuition fees are not covered by the scholarship.**
southafrica-france-scholarships.com.degree: Master's (2 years — granted for the full duration of the degree) and PhD (maximum 3 years, renewed annually on evidence of research progress)
southafrica-france-scholarships.com.description: The 2027 call of the France-South Africa Scholarship Programme is open, for students starting study in France in September 2027. All fields of study are eligible, with priority given to STEM and related humanities/social-science disciplines (digital technologies, AI, quantum technologies, biotechnology, health, environmental sciences, energy, low-carbon mobility, space, food systems, ICT). A shortlist is announced in December 2026 and final awards are confirmed in four waves between May and July 2027.
southafrica-france-scholarships.com.application_link: https://southafrica-france-scholarships.com — online application on the programme website; applicants must register, then select "final submission" before the deadline, after which the application cannot be modified

sciencespo.fr.official_source: Sciences Po (Paris) — Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at Sciences Po
sciencespo.fr.eligibility: All of: hold **citizenship of an African country** (dual citizenship including a non-African country is **not** eligible); be completing or already hold a Bachelor's degree from a listed partner university, **or** hold one from any institution plus a recognised bridge/mentoring programme from an approved organisation, **or** hold one plus current or past **UNHCR refugee status**; be **under 35 on 1 September** of the year the application is submitted; **not** already hold or be pursuing a Master's; be applying for the Mastercard program for the **first time**. **Not eligible:** students currently enrolled at Sciences Po; students currently enrolled in, or graduated from, a French higher-education institution. Applicants must also meet Sciences Po's academic requirements for their home-university country and be admitted to a **two-year** Master's at Sciences Po (dual-degree and one-year Master's are not eligible). Admission to the Master's and eligibility for the scholarship do not guarantee an interview or an award.
sciencespo.fr.degree: Two-year Master's (graduate level) at Sciences Po
sciencespo.fr.description: Information sessions run between **September and December 2026** (dates announced on the programme's LinkedIn and Instagram @sciencespo_mcfsp); the Sciences Po virtual Open House is **17 October 2026**. Selection is a multi-stage process: application review (barriers to education access, commitment to African development and transformative leadership, with particular weight given to young women, refugees/displaced persons and persons with disabilities), a ~25-minute Zoom interview for shortlisted admitted applicants, then a collective Scholarship Selection Committee decision. Offers are valid only for the academic year for which they are issued — deferring admission voids scholarship eligibility. AI use in the written assignments is explicitly discouraged and may lower evaluation. Contact: info.mcfsp@sciencespo.fr.
sciencespo.fr.application_link: https://admission.sciencespo.fr/applicants/login?lng=en (eligible applicants receive a fee-waiver code; non-eligible applicants may still apply by paying the standard application fee)
sciencespo.fr.benefits: The programme "**covers the full financial needs of selected Scholars**" and "provides comprehensive support throughout their two years of study at Sciences Po". **No euro amount is published on the page** — the amount comes from the Mastercard Foundation's own global programme documentation, so do not store a figure from this page.

semmelweis.hu.official_source: Semmelweis University — Center of International Training Programs, Registrar's Office (Budapest, Hungary). Merit-based scholarship introduced in 2025 for international students.
semmelweis.hu.eligibility: foreign nationals holding **student status** at Semmelweis University and originating from a country listed in Appendix 1 to the Call for Applications (Category 1 countries receive preference over Category 2); enrolled in a programme taught in German or English at the Faculty of General Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy, Health Sciences or the András Pető Faculty; studies begun in or after the first semester of academic year 2024/2025; student status established no earlier than September 2024 and no later than September 2027; at least two completed active semesters with outstanding academic performance and/or achievements in sport or the arts; not a recipient of the Stipendium Hungaricum or the Hungarian Diaspora Scholarship. Applicants must have a HUF-capable bank account registered as default in Neptun. Applicants who gave false information in a previous cycle are barred.
semmelweis.hu.benefits: awarded for one year and can be reapplied for after expiry (except students who have completed their studies). Unused annual amounts pass to the next student on the waiting list. Recipients must repay the amount plus statutory late-payment interest if they breach the scholarship contract; the full amount is repayable if they leave without completing the degree, are expelled, or terminate student status for non-compelling reasons, or behave in a way unbefitting the University. per academic year per student — Faculty of Medicine **HUF 2,000,000**; Faculty of Dentistry **HUF 2,000,000**; Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences **HUF 1,300,000**; Faculty of Health Sciences **HUF 900,000**; András Pető Faculty **HUF 2,900,000**. Paid in **12 equal monthly instalments** by bank transfer. If a KITA merit scholarship was also awarded that year, the Pannonia amount replaces it.
semmelweis.hu.degree: single long-cycle / undergraduate, master's (Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Health Sciences, András Pető Faculty)
semmelweis.hu.description: Merit-based scholarship, awarded on the basis of academic progress plus achievements in sport and the arts, supporting foreign nationals who already hold student status at Semmelweis University. Selection is made by a committee under Decision No. 99572/NHKK/2024 (Vice-Rector for International Studies, the five faculty deans, and the Students' Union/ISSA/DSVS chairpersons); appeals go to the Head of the Center of International Training Programs within 5 business days.
semmelweis.hu.application_link: https://semmelweis.hu/registrar/files/2026/02/Pannonia-In-25_26_palyazati-felhivas_EN.pdf  (Call for Applications; submission is via the Neptun "Requests" interface, not a web form)

anrfonline.in.official_source: Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), Department of Science and Technology, Government of India
anrfonline.in.eligibility: Indian / Indian-Origin scientists and engineers working **abroad** at the time of nomination, below 40 years of age, holding a PhD in Science/Engineering, Master's in Engineering/Technology, MD or equivalent with adequate professional experience and a proven outstanding research record. Nominee must not hold any permanent/tenure-track/contractual position in an Indian institute/university. Nomination must come from the head (or delegate) of the host institution; nominations by the candidate's own PhD supervisor or by the institute where the doctorate was earned are not accepted.
anrfonline.in.benefits: full financial support for the fellowship period (60 months from commencement), including regular extramural grants via the host institute; one international travel per year. Rs. 1,35,000 per month consolidated (including HRA) + research grant Rs. 7.00 lakh per annum + Rs. 60,000 per annum overhead charges to the host institute. The fellowship is taxable under Indian income-tax rules.
anrfonline.in.degree: Postdoctoral / research position (PhD or equivalent required) — not a taught degree programme.
anrfonline.in.description: Five-year, non-extendable, scientist-specific "reverse brain drain" fellowship established to attract brilliant Indian/Indian-Origin scientists and engineers working abroad to take up research positions in India. Fellows may work in any Indian university, academic institution or national laboratory (other than the institute where they earned their doctorate), and are recommended as equivalent to Scientist-D for travel/DA purposes. Grant for subsequent years is released against Statement of Expenditure, Utilisation Certificate and a progress report.
anrfonline.in.application_link: https://www.anrfonline.in/ANRF/Ramanujan_fellowship (register at https://www.anrfonline.in/ANRF/Registration , log in, Form Submission → Scheme: Ramanujan Fellowship, then "Send to Nominator")

ireland.ie.official_source: Ireland Fellows Programme — fully funded by the Irish Government and offered under the auspices of the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (Irish Aid); applications are handled by Irish embassies. Almost 4,000 people have studied in Ireland under it over the past 50+ years.
ireland.ie.benefits: one year of study in Ireland (study, research or professional training depending on strand); the programme has strand-specific additional awards — Kader Asmal (South Africa), Roger Casement (Nigeria and the Brazil/Colombia/Ecuador/Peru/Venezuela award), Seán McBride (Namibia), Archbishop Michael Courtney (Burundi), Frank Ferguson Fellowship in Engineering (Zambia), Cecilia Grierson (Argentina/Bolivia/Paraguay), Central America Award, and SIDS fellowships. the programme is fully funded by the Irish Government. Per-strand award amounts and scholarship values are published on the individual strand pages, not on the index page, and are not asserted here.
ireland.ie.degree: one year of study in Ireland at eligible level (strand-dependent; undergraduate and postgraduate)
ireland.ie.description: The Ireland Fellows Programme is one of Irish Aid's most longstanding programmes, offering people from around the world one year of study in Ireland. Applications are made through the applicant's local Irish embassy/UN office, and eligibility, courses and deadlines differ per strand and per country.

dcu.ie.official_source: Dublin City University (DCU) — DCU Global / Registry
dcu.ie.eligibility: Non-EU applicants. Undergraduates must apply to one of the **listed eligible 2027-28 programmes**; postgraduates to the listed eligible programmes in the relevant faculty. All non-EU applications to the listed programmes are automatically considered; no separate scholarship application.
dcu.ie.description: The 2027-28 page bundles five distinct awards: the DCU Merit Scholarship for Non-EU Students and four faculty/school international scholarships (Humanities & Social Sciences, Engineering & Computing, Business School, Science and Health). Each lists its own eligible programme codes for 2027-28. Recipients of one DCU international scholarship are not considered for another DCU scholarship. Page last updated ~1 day before research.
dcu.ie.benefits: Fee reductions on the **full-time 2027-2028 non-EU tuition fee**, differentiated by faculty/level: Humanities & Social Sciences postgraduate **EUR 2,000** / undergraduate **EUR 1,850**; Engineering & Computing postgraduate **EUR 4,400** / undergraduate **EUR 5,000**; Business School postgraduate **EUR 2,000** / undergraduate **EUR 2,800**; Science & Health postgraduate **EUR 5,000** (EUR 4,500 for the two Psychology MScs) / undergraduate **EUR 6,100** (EUR 3,100 for DC204 BSc in Athletic Therapy and Training). Plus a general **DCU Merit Scholarship for Non-EU Students** (partial, merit-based, amount not stated on the page).

rotary-yoneyama.or.jp.eligibility: Overseas students scheduled to enrol in a Japanese university or graduate school who have passed the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test (JLPT) at **N3 or above** at the time of application. Applicants must find and apply to a Japanese university/graduate school themselves before applying and must submit a copy of that admission application; graduate-school applicants must also submit a recommendation letter from a supervisor/professor at their target graduate school. Research students are not eligible. Applicants who plan to go on to a university outside Japan or to a language school are not eligible. If the applicant is rejected for admission to the issuing university, the scholarship is forfeited.
rotary-yoneyama.or.jp.degree: Undergraduate, Master's, Doctoral (research students explicitly excluded)
rotary-yoneyama.or.jp.description: Foundation-funded scholarship for overseas students enrolling in Japanese universities and graduate schools; applicants must already have applied to a Japanese institution and hold JLPT N3 or above. Selection results are notified by email by mid-March 2027.
rotary-yoneyama.or.jp.benefits: **Undergraduates JPY 100,000 per month; Master's students JPY 140,000 per month; Doctoral students JPY 140,000 per month.** Successful applicants may additionally receive a supplemental travel payment of **up to JPY 250,000** toward travel expenses to Japan, on submission of receipts and supporting documents after arrival. Payment begins April 2027 (April enrolment) or October/September 2027 (fall enrolment). Arrival in Japan before the designated month of admission is mandatory or eligibility is lost.

id:383.official_source: Erasmus University Rotterdam — Erasmus School of Economics
id:383.eligibility: full-time first-year master students (EEA and non-EEA) who have never been enrolled before as a full-degree Master student at any Dutch institution; admitted to and registered in Studielink for one of: Master Accounting, Auditing and Control; Master Econometrics and Management Science; Master Economics and Business; average final Bachelor result of at least 7.50 on a 1–10 scale; must submit a detailed financial statement; must complete the immigration procedure (instructed to send by May at the latest, official deadline 10 July). **Not applicable to current ESE Master students.**
id:383.description: Excellence scholarship for prospective first-year Master's students with outstanding results; applications reviewed after 1 February 2026, outcome by email by 13 March 2026. Only one type of scholarship is awarded per applicant.
id:383.benefits: maximum €17,500 for 2026-2027, comprising: full tuition-fee waiver (statutory or institutional); living allowance of €1,200/month = €14,400/year; one-off personal allowance €249; immigration fee of €228 waived. Only the living and personal allowances are transferred to the student's account.

id:384.official_source: Erasmus University Rotterdam — Erasmus MC (Erasmus University Medical Center)
id:384.eligibility: applying to one of the full-time Research Master's programmes at Erasmus MC — Health Sciences, Neuroscience or Molecular Medicine; average grade equivalent to a Dutch 8.0/10; belonging to one or more disadvantaged/underrepresented groups (limited financial/educational/social/health resources; refugee or newcomer status; ethnic/religious marginalisation; disability; first-generation student; LGBTQ+ identity with potential safety risks; reduced social capital); demonstrated community involvement and commitment to the Changemaker alumni network. The page's published **Nationality** field reads: "EEA".
id:384.description: Supports underrepresented students to pursue a Research Master's at Erasmus MC; awardees receive mentorship, training and access to a Changemaker alumni network. The eligible Research Master's programmes change each academic year.
id:384.benefits: €9,895 for costs of living and the statutory fee, for one year (Erasmus Trustfonds covers the statutory tuition fee and a €600/month living allowance); the TSH Changemaker Scholarship adds one year of housing in a Social Hub Residence; non-EU/EEA citizens on the institutional fee may receive a partial tuition-fee waiver from the school

student.universiteitleiden.nl.official_source: Leiden University — Leiden University Fund (LUF), in partnership with the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation
student.universiteitleiden.nl.eligibility: Students who have received an official letter of admission to a **one-year Master's programme at Leiden University**, or students enrolled in the **second year of a two-year Master's programme at Leiden University**. Nationalities: nationals of Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Syria, Tunisia, United Arab Emirates or Yemen. Eligible faculties: Archaeology, Humanities, Medicine/LUMC, Governance and Global Affairs, Law, Social and Behavioural Sciences, Science, ICLON, African Studies Centre, International Institute for Asian Studies.
student.universiteitleiden.nl.benefits: housing may be arranged via Leiden University with the housing fee paid directly from the scholarship. Students must fund their own travel and housing costs and the remainder of living costs, and must show proof of sufficient funds for the student visa/residence permit. An English test is a prerequisite of admission and its cost must be covered by the applicant. The above does not apply to LLM Advanced Studies programmes, which have higher tuition fees. **€30,000 for one academic year**, covering the Leiden University **tuition fee and housing fee (not the rent itself)**. The small remaining amount is paid to the student in monthly instalments. This is explicitly **not a full scholarship**.
student.universiteitleiden.nl.degree: Master's (one-year programme, or second year of a two-year Master's)
student.universiteitleiden.nl.description: The fund is intended for students who have demonstrated exceptional academic excellence and a strong motivation to promote Euro-Arab dialogue. The Lutfia Rabbani Foundation and the Leiden University Fund established the partnership in 2018.

id:386.official_source: Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), funded by the Justus & Louise van Effen Foundation
id:386.eligibility: An excellent international applicant (conditionally) admitted to one of the 2-year regular TU Delft MSc programmes (**not** an International Joint Education Programme); amongst the top 10% of graduates of the previous study programme; complete MSc application submitted before the scholarship deadline. Not eligible: TU Delft bachelor's students; international applicants with a Dutch bachelor's degree; students who have already started their MSc at TU Delft.
id:386.benefits: second-year scholarship allowances require at least 48 of 60 ECTS in the first year; may not be combined with any other partial or full scholarship funding Full tuition fees for the first year of a TU Delft MSc programme (statutory fee or institutional rate per registered nationality) **plus** a contribution to the living expenses
id:386.description: 16 scholarships per year (2 per faculty), financed by the legacy of Justus and Louise van Effen. Recipients informed by end of March 2027. Note: an archived version of the per-scheme page described the scholarship as covering "full tuition fees … for two years"; the **live** index page states full tuition for the **first year** plus a living-expense contribution — use the live wording above.

id:392.eligibility: Provisional or unconditional admission to a master programme received before February; excellent academic performance; excellent undergraduate grades; excellent English matching the chosen programme's admission requirements; availability for the whole programme; good health so Dutch health insurance can be arranged; nationality of a country listed in Appendix 1 (a long list including most of Africa, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, India, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Morocco, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Vietnam and others); no other means of financing.
id:392.description: University of Groningen fellowship for applicants from a defined list of developing and transition countries, covering the full cost of a one- or two-year master's; candidates are nominated by the Admission Office after admission rather than applying directly.
id:392.benefits: Grant awarded for a **1-year or 2-year Master's programme starting in September only**. Covers tuition fee, international travel, subsistence, books and health insurance. No monetary amount is published on the page. Only a limited number of grants can be issued each year.

kitlv.nl.official_source: KITLV — Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies
kitlv.nl.eligibility: KITLV invites scholars in the fields of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies; **a university affiliation is not required**. Applications must be in English and include a completed application form and a brief two-page CV, plus a proposal of the work to be carried out. Selection is by written assessment with no interviews; all applicants are informed of the outcome by the end of April.
kitlv.nl.benefits: KITLV provides office space, library and research facilities, and assists in finding suitable accommodation, although the accommodation itself is the fellow's own responsibility. Four fellowships are offered in this call: two for 1 September 2026 – 1 December 2026 and two for 1 December 2026 – 1 March 2027; each lasts three months. return air or train fare (economy class) to and from the Netherlands; reimbursement of accommodation costs in Leiden up to a maximum of **€2,000 per month** (rent, energy and service costs, on proof of payment); a monthly compensation for the higher cost of living in Leiden, awarded case by case. (source: same)
kitlv.nl.degree: not applicable — three-month visiting fellowship, no degree awarded
kitlv.nl.description: KITLV's second 2026 call for three-month visiting fellowships in Leiden, for researchers and professionals working on Southeast Asian and Caribbean studies. Four places are offered across two consecutive three-month periods.

id:395.eligibility: All non-EU/non-EEA countries. Applicant must hold a non-EU/non-EEA passport; not be eligible for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee for other reasons; hold (or be about to obtain) a Bachelor's degree achieved outside the Netherlands; hold no degrees achieved in the Netherlands and have received no previous education in the Netherlands (exchange programmes excluded if part of a Bachelor's obtained abroad); meet the English language requirement of the chosen Master's programme; be fully admitted to the English-taught Master's programme starting 1 September 2027 as stated in the formal letter of admission; be able to comply with Dutch visa conditions; enrol full-time. All English-taught Master's programmes are eligible except Erasmus Mundus and joint-degree Master's programmes.
id:395.benefits: Major tuition-fee reduction; Aon Student Insurance; can be combined with the NL Scholarship; continuation into a second year for two-year Master's programmes requires passing all first-year courses. Partial scholarship reducing the tuition fee to **€2,771** (amount to be confirmed) instead of €19,000 (depending on programme) for 2027/2028. The scholarship also covers visa, residence permit, health insurance and liability insurance costs (Aon Student Insurance). Living and study costs in the Netherlands are **not** covered.
id:395.description: A very selective, faculty-allocated partial scholarship for non-EEA students with outstanding study results on an English-taught Radboud Master's programme, funded by Radboud University's Profiling Fund. For 2027/2028 a maximum of **26** scholarships are available: Faculty of Arts (2), Faculty of Law (2), Nijmegen School of Management (5), Faculty of Philosophy, Theology and Religious Studies (1), Faculty of Science (9), Faculty of Social Sciences (7). Selection criteria: academic excellence, ambition, life experience/extracurricular activities, and quality of two reference letters (preferably academic).

id:429.eligibility: Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident intending to take up Singapore Citizenship; strong leadership qualities and potential; strong interest in safeguarding the safety and security of Singapore; good academic and Co-Curricular Activities records; GCE A-Levels, International Baccalaureate, Polytechnic, NUS High School or other high school diploma/certificate. Current undergraduates (not in final year) may also apply for a mid-term scholarship.
id:429.benefits: sponsorship of Master's and exchange programmes (if requirements are met); Vacation Attachment Programme; bond period of 4 years for local studies, 5 years for studies in non-English speaking countries, 6 years for studies in English speaking countries, starting when the recipient assumes official duty. Tuition fees and other approved charges; monthly overseas or local maintenance allowance (including accommodation); pre-studies allowance (settling in, warm clothing, computer); return economy class airfare (for selected tiers). Awarded at one of three tiers decided by the Scholarship Board: Singapore Government Scholarship (SGS), Local Merit Scholarship (LMS), Home Team Local Study Award (HTLSA).
id:429.degree: undergraduate, at a local or overseas university; most disciplines except medicine, dentistry and architecture (Law graduates will not be called to the Bar while serving in the Home Team)
id:429.description: Awarded to all-rounded individuals passionate about strengthening Singapore's safety and security in a civilian appointment, as a Generalist or as a Specialist (Commercial Affairs, Intelligence, Internal Security, Psychology).

id:430.official_source: Public Service Commission and Singapore Police Force (programme page hosted on the Ministry of Home Affairs site)
id:430.eligibility: Singapore Citizen; strong leadership qualities and potential; keen interest in serving in the Singapore Police Force; outstanding academic and Co-Curricular Activity records; GCE A-Levels, International Baccalaureate, Polytechnic, NUS High School or other high school diploma/certificate; must excel in Officer Cadet School. All MHA scholarships are open to male and female applicants; female applicants must apply early enough to prepare for Basic Military Training.
id:430.benefits: NS disruption cover; sponsorship of Master's and exchange programmes (if requirements are met); **full salary for the duration of studies including bonuses**; Vacation Attachment Programme; bond of 4 years (local studies), 5 years (studies in non-English speaking countries), 6 years (studies in English speaking countries), starting on the day official duty is assumed Tuition fees and other approved charges; monthly overseas or local maintenance allowance (including accommodation); pre-studies allowance; return economy class airfare (if studying overseas)
id:430.degree: undergraduate, local or overseas universities; most disciplines except medicine, dentistry and architecture (Law graduates will not be called to the Bar while serving in the SPF)
id:430.description: One of the most prestigious scholarships awarded by the Public Service Commission; a uniformed career track. Successful scholars are rotated through regular postings and may be placed on the Public Service Leadership Programme.

id:443.official_source: Singapore Management University — Office of Admissions and Financial Assistance
id:443.eligibility: Singapore Citizens; outstanding academic results; strong leadership capabilities and potential; excellent records in co-curricular and/or community activities; applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at SMU.
id:443.benefits: Growth opportunities allowance funds part or a combination of overseas community service projects and global exposure opportunities (overseas student exchanges/summer programmes and study missions); participation in Student Success Centre development opportunities. Waiver of annual subsidised tuition fees for regular terms (semesters 1 and 2) for up to 4 years, starting from Academic Year 2027-28. Growth opportunities allowance of S$12,000. Up to 35 SMU Merit Scholarships awarded each year. Bond-free.
id:443.description: An undergraduate award combining a full four-year tuition fee waiver with a growth opportunities allowance, for Singapore Citizens with outstanding academic results and strong leadership. Shortlisted applicants are invited to a panel interview.

id:454.eligibility: Must be a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland; must demonstrate academic talent and show interest in being in an educational environment; may be awarded only for a Master's programme ranked **first priority** on universityadmissions.se; must have applied for the Master's programme before the University Admissions deadline; must meet the programme's entry requirements, with the application fee and complete supporting documents received by University Admissions before the deadline. Excluded programmes: Joint Nordic Master's Programme in Environmental Law; Master's Programme in Biology NABiS Nordic Master in Biodiversity and Systematics; Master's Programme in Evolutionary Biology – MEME; Master's Programme in Implementation, Transformative Learning and Sustainability; Master's Programme in Religion in Peace and Conflict; Master's Programme in Transformative Game Design; Master's Programme in Turkic Studies.
id:454.description: Tuition-fee waiver for fee-paying international Master's applicants who rank an Uppsala programme first and meet the academic-talent criteria.
id:454.benefits: Covers the **full tuition fee** for an international Master's programme at Uppsala University. It does **not** cover living expenses. Funded by the Swedish Council for Higher Education. Scholarships are highly competitive — only about **2%** of applicants are granted one. No fixed SEK amount is published (the fee varies by programme).

mau.se.eligibility: Must have applied for an **English-taught** master's programme at Malmö University, applied **in the first admissions round**, chosen Malmö as **first choice on University Admissions (ranked #1 of 4)**, been **admitted to that first-choice programme**, and be required to pay tuition fees. Admitted students receive further instructions after the Notification of Selection Results. No extra documents are required.
mau.se.description: Each year Malmö University offers a limited number of scholarships to qualified master's students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are liable to pay tuition fees. Selection is based on previous academic excellence, the experience described in the CV, and the applicant's ability to motivate social engagement through their chosen programme. Applicants are notified of the outcome by the end of April.
mau.se.benefits: Covers **partial or up to the full tuition fee**; explicitly **does not cover living expenses or other costs**. Students admitted to two-year programmes retain the scholarship for the second year if they complete year 1 and meet the progression criteria (minimum 22.5 credits/semester, minimum 45 credits/academic year). Only a few students are granted scholarships each year.

lunduniversity.lu.se.eligibility: Must be, or have been, a student at an ARUA member university in one of the listed countries; must be a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland and be required to pay tuition fees at Lund; must have submitted a correct, complete and timely application for an international degree programme at Lund; must have selected Lund University as first choice at universityadmissions.se. Financial situation is not considered — the scheme is merit-based only.
lunduniversity.lu.se.degree: Bachelor's and Master's international degree programmes at Lund University
lunduniversity.lu.se.description: A selective, merit-based scholarship for high-achieving African students from ARUA member universities. Applications require a one-minute "scholarship motivation video" hosted on an open platform. Results are sent in the same email as the Lund University Global Scholarship results. Applicants may apply for ARUA in addition to LUGS and Swedish Institute scholarships, but only one ARUA Scholarship per application round.
lunduniversity.lu.se.benefits: A percentage of tuition fees up to a maximum of 90% (exact percentage depends on the available budget of the programme/faculty concerned). Does NOT cover living costs; recipients must meet Swedish Migration Agency living-expense requirements.

id:466.official_source: University of Zurich — Student Financial Aid Office (SIB UZH)
id:466.eligibility: Enrolled at the University of Zurich and in an acute financial emergency without any debt. Must be able to plausibly guarantee repayment **within six months**. May be applied for a maximum of once per semester.
id:466.benefits: Processing takes approximately 6–8 working days; no bureaucratic red tape; bridges gaps while awaiting a cantional scholarship. Short-term loans are not for paying off debts. **Maximum CHF 6,000 per application**; interest-free. Repayment is plausible-guarantee based and must be made within six months; unpaid loans are immediately sent to a debt collector.
id:466.degree: All enrolled degree levels (first-degree programmes; UZH does not support PhD)
id:466.description: UZH's interest-free hardship loan for students in acute, debt-free financial emergency; intended as a temporary bridge, typically an advance on a scholarship or on tuition fees.

id:467.official_source: Ministry of Education, Republic of China (Taiwan)
id:467.eligibility: An international scholar who is (1) a PhD student at an overseas government-approved and registered public or private university/tertiary college; or (2) a postdoctoral research fellow awarded a PhD by any such institution, in Taiwan or overseas, now undertaking research at an overseas institution. Must **not** hold an ROC passport; not be currently visiting/residing/studying/interning/teaching/researching in Taiwan; not be receiving other Taiwanese government or institutional funding for the research; not be an exchange student under a Taiwan–overseas cooperation agreement during the proposed research period; and not have received an STRA in the last 5 years. Scholars from mainland China, Hong Kong and Macao are excluded. Research topic must relate to Taiwan in a humanities, social science, culture/art field, or related comparative research.
id:467.description: STRA placements run for **2 to 6 months** and are intended to let international scholars undertake short-term research in Taiwan while increasing understanding of Taiwanese culture and society. Applications must reach the host institution by 30 September each year; the host institution then submits the nomination.
id:467.benefits: Monthly research allowance of **NTD 25,000** for a PhD student or **NTD 40,000** for a postdoctoral fellow, **plus an economy-class return airfare** on the most direct route between the fellow's place of residence and Taiwan.

eastwestcenter.org.official_source: East-West Center (Honolulu, Hawai'i, USA) — the fellowship supports graduate study at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa.
eastwestcenter.org.eligibility: citizens or permanent residents of the **United States**, or of listed countries in the Pacific Region (American Samoa, Australia, Cook Islands, Easter Island/Rapa Nui, Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, French Polynesia, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Northern Marianas, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tokelau, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu, Wallis & Futuna), Southeast Asia (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Vietnam), South Asia (Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Iran, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka) and East Asia (China, Hong Kong, Japan, Macau, Mongolia, North Korea, South Korea, Russia, Taiwan). Must have obtained a 4-year bachelor's degree or equivalent from an accredited U.S. institution or a recognised institution abroad before the award starts; minimum GPA of 3.0 (4.0 = A) or equivalent over the last four semesters and in all post-baccalaureate work. Priority is given to applicants committed to the development of the Indo-Pacific region and to fields relevant to the Center's goals.
eastwestcenter.org.benefits: housing in an East-West Center residence hall for the academic year on a single-occupancy basis; Community Building Institute and advising at the start of the award; alumni and Foundation scholarships may supplement a Graduate Degree Fellowship; alumni are also considered for EWCA Alumni and Foundation scholarships. full-time graduate tuition and fees up to the equivalent of the general tuition charged for post-baccalaureate students at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa toward master's or doctoral study; plus partial funding toward incidental expenses. Funding for field study and conference presentations is offered on a competitive basis. No single dollar figure is published; awards are made annually and initially for one academic year (fall + spring), renewable for one additional academic year subject to funding availability, satisfactory progress and Center requirements. Fellowships do **not** provide support for spouses/dependents.  (source for the award breakdown: https://www.eastwestcenter.org/education/ewc-graduate-degree-fellowship/gdf-award-details — this page could not be loaded directly (navigation timeout); its text was read from the live index of that same official EWC URL.)
eastwestcenter.org.description: The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship funds master's and doctoral study at the University of Hawai'i at Mānoa for citizens of the U.S., Asia and the Pacific. Applicants not already classified as graduate students at UH Mānoa must also apply to the university for the following fall semester by 1 December; supporting documents for both the UH admissions office and the department must be completed by 10 January.

phikappaphi.org.official_source: The Honor Society of Phi Kappa Phi
phikappaphi.org.eligibility: Must be an **active (dues paid) member through April 15, 2027**, or have accepted the invitation to join and be initiated by **June 30, 2027** (membership status verified by phone, (800) 804-9880 ext. 235). Seeking full-time enrolment in a graduate/professional school programme **beginning between May 1, 2027 and February 1, 2028**. Must not have completed **more than 9 hours of semester credits** of graduate study in any field at the application deadline (applicants with 10 or more graduate credits on or before April 15 are ineligible). Must not be a sitting Phi Kappa Phi board member, divisional vice president, member of the Fellowship Award committee, or Society employee at the time of application. Each active chapter may select **one** local candidate to compete Society-wide. Selection is assessed on academic achievement (transcripts, honours, awards, research experience, creative work samples), service and leadership on and off campus, letters of recommendation, personal statement and career goals, work sample, and acceptance/application to an approved graduate or professional programme.
phikappaphi.org.degree: Graduate — first year of a graduate or professional degree (master's, doctoral or professional)
phikappaphi.org.description: The Society's flagship award, made possible by chapter endorsement. Fellows go on to study at some of the nation's top graduate schools. Applicants must be nominated by their local chapter, which selects one candidate for the Society-wide competition.
phikappaphi.org.application_link: https://apply.phikappaphi.org/Awards/ (portal opens 15 December 2026; the completed PDF, official transcripts, work sample and two letters of recommendation are then submitted to your local chapter by that chapter's deadline)
phikappaphi.org.benefits: **40 Fellowships of USD 8,500 each, six at USD 15,000 each, and two at USD 35,000 each** per year. The Fellowship Program was established in 1932 and is awarded to members entering the first year of graduate or professional study across all academic disciplines.

id:480.official_source: Harvard College — Griffin Financial Aid Office (The President & Fellows of Harvard College)
id:480.eligibility: All prospective students regardless of citizenship must submit the CSS Profile and an IDOC Packet; US citizens and permanent residents must also submit the FAFSA. Applicants must submit the actual 2025 tax return (signed) for student and both parents, business/trust/estate documents where applicable, and translated documentation where documents are not in English. IDOC cannot be accessed until the CSS Profile is complete.
id:480.description: Harvard College's need-based financial aid application for the 2027-2028 school year. Applicants must file the 2027-2028 CSS Profile via the College Board (Harvard code 3434), the 2027-2028 FAFSA (Harvard code E00468) if applicable, and documents through the College Board IDOC service.
id:480.benefits: Need-based financial aid; no fixed amount published. Financial aid decisions are issued around 1 April for Restrictive Early Action and Regular Decision applicants.

global.utexas.edu.official_source: The University of Texas at Austin — Texas Global / International Student and Scholar Services (ISSS)
global.utexas.edu.eligibility: Applicants must already be **enrolled full-time at UT Austin** and must have **completed an entire course of study for two academic semesters** at UT Austin (minimum cumulative GPA above 2.0 undergraduate / 3.0 graduate), and demonstrate financial need or the award-specific criteria. Specific awards add conditions: e.g. STEM Scholarship limited to Cockrell Engineering, Dell Medical School and most College of Natural Sciences programmes; TAMS and GNS are administered on behalf of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board. Applications are submitted via the university-wide **LASSO** system.
global.utexas.edu.benefits: Scholarships are **one-time awards and are not guaranteed in subsequent years**. 14% of cash awards is withheld for US tax purposes unless a tax treaty applies or the recipient is a resident alien. Cash awards are applied automatically to outstanding UT debts, with the excess paid to the student's direct deposit account. Varies per award — spring/summer: Carlos and Clara Quintanilla USD 5,000; Ethel Loving de Diaz USD 4,500; SIAWE USD 3,500; Dr. David Nilsson USD 2,000; General ISSS Financial Aid (cash, amount not stated); IEFS (amount not stated); TAMS (non-resident tuition waiver). Fall/academic year: STEM Scholarship USD 4,800; African Leadership Bridge USD 5,000 (USD 2,500 per semester) plus non-resident tuition waiver; Iimura Peace USD 5,000; Jerry D. Wilcox USD 3,500; Khalid Alhilali USD 2,500; General ISSS Financial Aid (cash); IEFS; TAMS; Good Neighbor Scholarship (one year's tuition — fall, spring and summer — for students born in and resident in a Western Hemisphere nation; excludes fees, health insurance and the ISSS support fee).
global.utexas.edu.description: ISSS administers a set of distinct named scholarships for international students, split into spring/summer-term awards (Oct 1 – Nov 1 window) and fall/academic-year awards (Feb 1 – Mar 1 window). Applicants search "ISSS" in LASSO.

id:494.official_source: Latvian state scholarship — State Education Development Agency (VIAA), which operates the "Study in Latvia" national portal. Awarded under Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No. 68 of 24 January 2012 "Procedures for Granting Scholarships to Foreigners".
id:494.eligibility: permanent residents of 39 eligible countries (citizens of more than 30 partner countries); Bachelor's students must already have completed at least one academic year at any higher education institution; Master's/PhD students may come from any previous HEI; the applicant must choose a study programme at a Latvian HEI **and** obtain a confirmation letter from that HEI (on the unified template, provided by the designated contact person) before applying; documents must be translated into Latvian or English; a scholarship cannot be combined with other grants.
id:494.benefits: awarded for up to 10 months (Bachelor's/Master's) or up to 11 months (PhD); maximum of two terms within one study cycle; the award decision is notified by e-mail in June. A separate summer-school strand exists under the same 1 Feb – 1 Apr call, but funds are transferred to the organisers and no money is paid to winners. **EUR 500 per month** for Bachelor's and Master's students and **EUR 700 per month** for PhD students. Per Cabinet Regulation No. 68 ¶6, as amended by Cabinet Regulation No. 298 of 26 May 2026, second-cycle higher-education programmes are set at EUR 500/month. The scholarship does **not** fully cover expenses: tuition, living costs and other expenses must be covered personally, and travel to/from Latvia and insurance are not covered. Average tuition fees run EUR 2,800–15,000/year.
id:494.description: Latvia's state scholarship for international students from partner countries to study at Latvian higher education institutions, administered by VIAA through a single annual open call. Applications require a HEI confirmation letter, Europass CV, motivation letter, proof of education, two letters of recommendation (signed within the last 6 months), a study plan and a language certificate.
id:494.application_link: https://scholarships.viaa.gov.lv/en/login  (online electronic application system; registration required)
